reviews.text:
It's a 2 storey historical building where they have a small museum on Level 2 on the history of Sun Cake and a cafe (closes at 4pm), then on Level 1 it's their retail store and DIY Sun Cake workshop experience. Which was what I'm really here for.

They have several sessions a day and you'll need to pre-book online via their website (a Google form) and they'll confirm the session via WhatsApp as they need a minimum group size to proceed. The workshop costs NTD300 per person and you get to bring home 6 mini sun cakes that you make.

The ingredients are all prepared for you, the pastry chef just brings us through the process of rolling out the dough, wrapping in the malt candy then pressing it to shape. Sound like simple steps but this essentially took an hour. After which, the instructor helps put them to bake and 30 mins later, it comes out nicely packed into a box shaped like the building itself.

Here, they don't use lard in the dough, but instead, good quality french butter, so it's vegetarian-friendly and I think butter adds a different layer of fragrance, that still lingers on my fingers.

Unfortunately I didn't get to take photos or videos as the dough is pretty oily and the workshop was done in a group of 18 pax, it was kind of hard to constantly pause and clean my hands to use the phone to take photos. Having said so, I enjoyed the experience very much, the instructor was also very friendly and funny. And tasting your own bakes, fresh out of the oven is simply amazing. Flaky, soft, not too sweet. A must do in Taichung!

The Taiwan Sun Cake Museum is a small but delightful stop for anyone interested in the history and craftsmanship behind one of Taichung’s most famous pastries. Located in the heart of the city, this museum offers a charming glimpse into the origins of sun cakes (taiyang bing), a beloved Taiwanese treat known for its flaky crust and sweet malt filling.

The exhibits showcase traditional baking tools, historical photos, and detailed explanations about the evolution of sun cakes. Visitors can also watch demonstrations of how these pastries are made, adding an interactive element to the experience. Some workshops even allow guests to try their hand at making their own sun cakes, which is a fun and memorable activity.

While the museum is relatively small, it’s well-organized and informative. The staff are friendly and eager to share their knowledge. At the end of the visit, there’s an opportunity to sample and purchase freshly made sun cakes, making it a perfect place for food lovers and those looking for an authentic local souvenir.

Sun Cake 太阳饼  is a Most Traditional Iconic Chinese Pastry of Taiwan Taichung. Its the Type of Thing that Visitors to Taichung will always buy as Souvenirs.  There are Many Pastry Shops Everywhere in Taichung that sells this, and the one I'm showcasing here I feel is Slightly Unique among them because its also a Museum dedicated to it.

The Exterior of the Building looks Old and Historical.  Consisting of 2 Floors, the 1st Floor houses a Gift Shop  and interestingly a Bakery,  while the 2nd Floor is the Actual Museum itself.

Unfortunately when I was there, there was some sort of Local Organized Event,  similar to our Singapore CC RC Event of sorts and the Museum was inaccessible to the Public while the Event was going on.  So I didn't have the chance to visit the Museum Side of the Place.

The Bakery located on the 1st Floor

If I remember correctly from what the Staffs told me, you can book a Guided Tour which costs about TWD300 (S$12.20)  which will include a Guided Tour of the Museum and you will also get the Chance to Learn to Bake an Actual Sun Cake yourself.

While I didn't take up this offer (partly due to the Current Ongoing RC Event they have), The Instructor seemed like a Very Joyous Friendly Chap  although I think its only conducted in Mandarin. So feel free to sign up for it if you're interested.

The Pastry Gift Shop

Operates just like any Regular Gift Shop, this of course sells Sun Cakes in Various Different Flavours.  You can take a look at the Photo Collection to get an Idea of the Types available and their Prices.

The Staffs are Very Friendly and Polite.  What I particularly love about this place is that as a Solo Traveller, I don't have to buy an Entire Box of Sun Cakes if I just want to try.  They sell them in Individual Ala-Carte Pieces too.

In addition, if you would like to dine in, there is a Small Area with a Table and some Benches for you to Comfortably enjoy your Sun Cakes.

Sun Cake 太阳饼 (原味, Original) = TWD40

As you can see in the Photos, outwardly, Sun Cake looks Similar to Wife Cake. They're the same type of Round Round Flaky sort of Traditional Chinese Pastry.  Just like its Namesake, its Bright in Colour.  Sun Cake is Noticeably Softer in Comparison and has a Slight Buttery Aroma.

When you bite into it, you will find that its 松松软软 Ultra Airy and Flakey.  Because of how Soft this was, I feel this would also appeal to Elderly Folks too.  From a Baking Standpoint, I find the Layering to be Superb.  You need a Certain Amount of Skill and Technique to be able to pull this off.

Another thing I really like about Sun Cakes is how Subtle Sweet the Inner Filling is.  It uses a Familiar Sticky Sweet Maltose based filling you'd expect from a Pastry of this type but the Sweetness is Very Delicate and Light.

Conclusion and Closing Thoughts

At TWD40 (S$1.70 Each) for the Sun Cake is not particularly Cheap, and because there are Many Pastry Shops that sell this Iconic Pastry, there may be Cheaper ones out there.  What I do appreciate is that I can buy just 1 Piece to Try instead of committing to buy a Whole Box of them.

I don't usually eat such Traditional Chinese Pastries often, but I do enjoy this for its Very Delicate, Flakey Skin and Light Sweetness.  If you enjoy such Pastries, I feel you willl most likely enjoy this too.

What is interesting was the Whole Place itself.  Although I did not have the chance to visit the Museum, I feel it is still worth to come visit if you come to Taichung to not only buy the Iconic Sun Cake  but to learn abit of History and even try to make one yourself if you are so inclined.

If you are interested in Taichung's Most Iconic Traditional Chinese Pastry, this is a Place that I feel is Worth a Visit.

The "Avalokitesvara Riding a Dragon" was built in 1979 (the 68th year of the Republic of China) and is located between the two towers of the Chunqiu Pavilion in Lianchitan. Its origin is due to a myth: According to legend, Guanyin Bodhisattva once appeared in the clouds riding a dragon, and instructed believers to build a statue in this form between the Chunqiu Pavilion to "compassionately save the suffering and save the lost."

### 🏯 **Architectural Features**

- **Giant Dragon Statue**:
The total length is 25.7 feet (about 78 meters) and the height is 3.6 feet (about 11 meters). The dragon's body is winding like flying in the clouds. Guanyin holds a pure bottle and stands on the dragon's back. On both sides stand Shancai Tongzi and Longnu.

- **Secret Realm in the Dragon's Belly**:
The dragon's mouth is the entrance, and there are 108 steps in the belly. The wall is painted with reliefs of Guanyin's 32 incarnations and 18 Arhats. The exit at the end of the tunnel faces Wuli Pavilion, forming a worship route of "entering the dragon's throat and exiting the fairyland".

### ⚡️ **Cultural anecdotes**

1. **Controversy over the origin of the appearance of the God**:
During the August 7 flood in Taiwan in 1959, the image of "Dragon-riding Guanyin Appearing" was circulated among the people. It was later confirmed to be a remake of the 19th-century Japanese painter Harada Naojiro's oil painting "Dragon-riding Guanyin". In 1984, the color version copied by Taiwanese painter Cai Zhongxun became more widely circulated.

2. **The mystery of Feng Shui balance**:
It is said that because the imperial palace (Yuan Emperor Temple) in the southeast of Lianchi Lake was too majestic, the Spring and Autumn Pavilion was eclipsed by it. Believers then built a dragon-riding statue to balance the Feng Shui and enhance the visual impact of the religious landmark.

### 🌿 **Current situation and experience**

Open to the public for free, under the night lights, the dragon's body and the reflection of the lake are like a dream. Combining the lotus scenery of Wuliting and the palace outline of Chunqiu Pavilion, it has become a "mythological scene" that must be visited in Lianchi Lake.

Located between the Spring and Autumn Pavilions (Spring Pavilion and Autumn Pavilion), on the Half Moon Pond, it presents a spectacular image of Guanyin Bodhisattva riding on a dragon. It is said that Guanyin once "appeared on a dragon" in the clouds and instructed believers to erect a statue based on the appearance. Therefore, this statue was built to show the meaning of compassion and salvation.

reviews.text: 5 stars to all the staff in this hotel: from the front desk to restaurant crew to the cleaning crew.  Everyone was delightful and courteous. No information about the hotel was given during check-in (locations of facilities, opening times, check-out time, etc) but left to us to consciously ask about.

We had a terrible experience at this hotel in May 2025. The facilities are lovely, but the service we received from the front desk service staff was appalling.

We accidentally double booked with two booking platforms (Agoda and Booking.com) and thought we'd cancelled the Agoda booking before we arrived in Tainan. On arrival, we were told we had still two bookings and a male assistant manager named Jayden Cai said that they would assist us to cancel the Agoda booking. The following day, no one contacted us and when we followed up at the front desk in the evening, we were informed that there was nothing the hotel could do to assist us with a refund from Agoda. This was a lie, as Agoda advised was that the hotel could authorise Agoda to cancel the booking and issue a refund. After a lot of pushing at the hotel, we managed to get half the booking fee back the following day, but then the situation got worse.

We had made two international calls from our hotel room to our bank (approximately one hour in total), to clarify the double booking issue as the hotel were so unhelpful. The hotel charged us NT$4,200 for these calls which was extremely expensive. However, there were no notices or visible rate information regarding international call charges inside the room before we used the phone. Only after we complained did the hotel write a line in their online 'precautions'  information page to say that enquiries regarding external call charges should be referred to the front desk. I have photo evidence of the before and after information sheets. After a further complaint, a customer service manager, Mina Wu, agreed to refund the second half of the Agoda booking, but we would still have to pay the phone charge, with a small discount.

When we checked out, the Agoda refund still hadn't come through, so we had to call Agoda to request that it be processed on the spot. We were treated with disdain by the hotel staff at the front desk, which made the whole experience very stressful and uncomfortable.

I do not recommend this hotel. The entire situation could have been avoided had the hotel authorised Agoda to issue a refund when we arrived, as they were able to do this. Instead, the staff were obstructive and dishonest about the refund and changing the room information about the telephone charges. It gave us an uncomfortable experience, very poor impression of the hotel and completely ruined our holiday in Tainan.

Expecting a comfortable experience, but we ended up incredibly disappointed. Aside from the excellent service from the concierge team, every other part of our stay fell short.

Check-in
The check-in process was unorganized and lacked clarity. The staff member assisting us didn’t provide basic information about our stay. We had to ask for everything ourselves, and even then, her responses felt unsure and lacked confidence. While she was friendly, she clearly needs to improve her knowledge and be more proactive in sharing essential details with guests.

Concierge
The best part of our stay was the concierge service. The employee working the evenings of June 11 and 12 was friendly, professional, and helpful. He gave us useful information about the hotel facilities and even escorted us to the elevator. Another staff member working with him on June 12 was also great. Although we didn’t experience other concierge services, both of them stood out and deserve recognition for their excellent service. Overall, the concierge team was consistently excellent throughout our stay.

Lobby restaurant
Our experience with the lobby restaurant staff was quite the opposite. On the mornings of June 12 and 13, a female employee with a ponytail and straight bangs was noticeably rude and unfriendly. On the first day, she was stationed at the entrance checking in guests. On the second, she was clearing plates. Her attitude made us feel uncomfortable, like she didn’t want to be there at all. It’s disappointing to be treated this way when you’re simply trying to enjoy breakfast. If staff aren’t willing to engage with guests professionally, they shouldn’t be on the floor.

Front desk
The front desk team needs the most improvement. Although they were overall friendly, it felt like they were either quite new or simply not motivated to improve their service. In addition to the underwhelming check-in, we approached the front desk on the evening of June 12 and the morning of June 14 to confirm some details, but the staff seemed unsure, unengaged, and unable to provide clear or accurate answers.

Room condition and amenities
While we understand the hotel promotes environmental sustainability, the lack of bottled water was inconvenient. Each floor only has one water dispenser, which isn’t ideal when you’re in a rush or just need a quick refill. The room door was also extremely heavy and shut very quickly, which actually hurt our hands when we weren’t expecting it, guests should be warned. In one of the rooms, we also noticed mold around the air conditioning vent, which was both unpleasant and unacceptable.

Breakfast
We booked a 4-night stay with breakfast included daily, but the food never changed. The variety was limited and the overall taste was just average. By the second day, it already felt repetitive and unexciting. Even the simplest egg dishes we tried, sunny side up, omelet, and eggs benedict were poorly cooked.

Laundry
We used the self-service laundry every day. Each time, we registered at the counter as required. We had used the facility more than 6 times during our stay and not once did we go past the stated closing time. We always finished and collected our laundry well before 10pm. Despite this, every time we showed up around 9pm, the staff would repeat the same warning that they close at 10pm and made us feel like we were causing a problem. It became increasingly frustrating. If staff want to leave early, then the hotel shouldn’t advertise the laundry as open until 10pm.

The hotel is rated as a 4-star property but promotes itself as 5-star. Aside from the concierge team, the service felt more like what you’d expect from a 2 or 3-star hotel. Even the breakfast, which we had enjoyed during our last visit, was a disappointment this time in both quality and variety.

Based on how things are, it doesn’t seem like the hotel takes feedback seriously. I’m sharing this so other guests can consider these points before booking.

I had two really relaxing nights here. The vibe was awesome. Everything was new, and the receptionists were all very kind.

However, it gave me a fright the bed made huge noises every time I turn. And there was a smell coming from the toilet pipe. I had to keep the toilet door shut.

Great hotel, very clean and modern. Very well located. Elevator is a bit small but ok. Breakfast was ok too. Would go back!

We have been like a regular customer and have stayed at this hotel a lot of times with my family already in the past this place was very very good.
The food,the service,the cleanliness,but…it fell off hard. Recently when I visited this hotel I found out that the breakfast standards dropped so much,it was still edible but…it wasn’t as good u know? I’m also about to say something that might make you guys freak out and not want to stay here, there was a glass shard on the floor. It wasn’t big but I stepped on it and my leg hurt,maybe the staff didn’t vacuum the floor thoroughly but I’m just saying that a child might get hurt, so…and room even didn’t provide toilet paper roll. Anyways ,the whole room is a square bro,other hotel are like rectangle and shit but this room is a square which make it so claustrophobic! Anyway on to the good part, The hair dryer was so nice! It wasn’t very hot like your scalp was burning when you used it. And as you might know,there are earthquakes and so electricity might be cut off and they provided a literal torchlight!
First time! Like they all say safety first am I right? Another thing is that the lobby has a little book to write or draw some stuff to show that you have visited and stayed in that hotel which is so cute. Overall ,this place is quite ok.

A very cozy hotel located in an excellent location. The breakfast they provided was excellent and very worth it. Our rooms were super clean and the shower was spacious. We also especially liked the provided shampoo and body wash, they had a really nice scent.

The staff went above and beyond to accommodate us during typhoon Gaemi. We were in Hualien the day before, and because of the typhoon we were unable to commute to the hotel on that day. The hotel staff allowed us to change our dates of stay last minute free of charge and we are extremely thankful for that.

reviews.text: A comfortable stay. It seemed a bit dated on first arrival (old fashioned lift/elevator and a key for the room) but the room looked recently renovated and had everything I needed. The breakfast is very good with a wide range of choice. The pillows, though, are very firm!

Despite its age and reliance on keys for room access, Hotel Tainan maintains a high level of cleanliness and upkeep. Staff are exceptional. Conveniently located as it is within a short walking distance from Tainan Railway Station, providing easy access to the city’s transportation.

Hotel Tainan is well located, iconic and has a retro yet personal feel. Rooms are clean with excellent and polite services from staff. I am especially impressed by their attention to details. Restaurants are good with an unexpected delicious international buffet spread. A very happy value for money stay. 👍❤️

DO NOT BOOK – Unprofessional and Possibly a Scam

I had an extremely disappointing and stressful experience with Tainan Hotel. I booked my stay months in advance and had been in regular communication with the hotel via WhatsApp the entire time. Everything seemed confirmed and in order—until just 5 days before my arrival, they cancelled my booking without informing me.

To make things worse, they attempted to charge my credit card before my check-in date and asked me to pay in advance months ago, which is against Booking.com policies. I only found out my reservation had been canceled because I checked myself. No email, no message, no explanation.

I immediately contacted Booking.com, who confirmed that the hotel was in clear violation of their policies and that the situation was mishandled on the hotel's end.

Now, I'm left without accommodation days before arriving in Vietnam during peak tourist season, with flights already booked. Finding a last-minute room during this busy time is not only difficult but also far more expensive.

This kind of behavior is completely unprofessional and unacceptable. It shows a lack of integrity, accountability, and basic customer service.

Avoid Tainan Hotel at all costs. They are not reliable, and based on my experience, they may be running a scam. Don’t risk ruining your travel plans.
It’s a clean budget hotel with an included  breakfast buffet and evening snack. Don’t expect anything luxurious there is a Starbucks in the lobby. The staff is extremely polite and helpful.

reviews.text: At this price point, it has to be one of the absolute worst Hotels I have ever been at. The hotel is apparently a little older, which is not a bad thing, but the Shangri La is just worn down badly. Everything looks old, from the rooms to the pool area. And the rooms are just disgusting. We had to change rooms twice because both rooms smelled extremely moldy. The third room didn’t smell moldy, but after the initial chemical smell disappeared, the room started to smell like an old dirty bar. Matching this smell, the bathroom now started smelling like someone smoked in there. Don’t get me wrong, the staff is super friendly and they try their best, but they can’t magically change a rotten hotel that only people without the sense of smell can safely stay at. We got two more nights to go and seriously think about leaving early. If we could get our money back, we would leave as soon as possible. Calling this a five star hotel got to be some kind of prank. Do yourself a favor, go somewhere else!

This Shangri-la was a pleasant surprise to me, location is ideal, fantastic service and good attention to details. The restaurant staff were kind and concerned about me as an Indian on the kind of meat offered, food choices and any allergies to food types.
The rooms that I got had a fantastic view, and the room service and house keeping is excellent.
One can exchange currency at the reception desk and cabs are available just outside of the hotel which makes it convenient to visit any given location. The local train station is bang next door and a shopping mall within the vicinity.
As this hotel is situated around the local university, there are many local eateries that offer lots of different cuisine choices.

Had a wonderful stay here! The hospitality was warm and welcoming, making the entire experience comfortable and pleasant. The café was definitely a highlight — especially the India counter run by Chef Akki. The food was delicious, and the service was excellent.

A special mention to Dora, Amber, Naomi, and Yan from the Horizon Club — their hospitality and service were truly fantastic. They were always attentive, friendly, and made every interaction feel personal and genuine.

Overall, it was a lovely stay filled with good vibes, great food, and amazing people. Highly recommended!

Consistently Excellent: The Gold Standard of Hospitality (Diamond Member for Life!)

Shangri-La Tainan is truly my preferred residence when traveling. I've stayed here for more than 100 nights now, and the experience never falters.

As a Diamond member (achieved after 50 nights), I especially appreciate the complimentary Horizon Club Lounge access, which elevates every stay and makes the property a genuine urban sanctuary.

The team effortlessly creates a serene, dream-like atmosphere that makes you forget the world outside—they truly embody the essence of the "Shangri-La" name. This attention to detail extends to personal touches, like the lovely mocktail and cake they served me today to celebrate the Moon Festival in Taiwan.

A special shout-out to Miss. Dora Amber in the Horizon Club today, October 6, for her outstanding service and genuine care. She is a true asset!

From the warm welcome to the luxurious rooms, everything is handled with genuine care and professionalism. My loyalty speaks for itself; if there's a Shangri-La nearby, I'm booking it! A flawless experience, every single time.

Daniel makes excellent drinks during happy hour! This evening he made shadow of flower cocktails and they were spectacular! Naomi was our waitress and she was very attentive and her service was exceptional! The rest of the team Penny, Yan, and Amber worked great as a team to care for every guest. Thank you!

reviews.text:
A beautiful hotel. The rooms are spacious and the window is very large. Very quiet, which is nice after flying 12+hours to visit relatives.
The service is great and the staff are wonderful. The location is nice since Mitsukoshi is right next door and they have everything you may need and then some. It makes dining easy also.

Excellent check in service, early arrival at 8:30 🕣 am and the Receptionist Ryan helped with finishing the check in process, answered all my questions with friendly smiling face and written notes of my questions. WONDERFUL service!

Waiting for the call to get into the room if any availability possible, happy to catch up with friend and attend the event first!!!

We booked this hotel for 2 nights but as soon as we both arrived we both noticed the room had a strong musty odor. But we both avoided saying anything to each other to try and make the best of the situation. But after awhile it was just unbearable and we had to call down to see if we could change our room. Max, the manager on the night shift came upstairs to assess the room condition and agreed to a change.  It was very late and we had traveled for almost an entire day so we were very exhausted. Max was very helpful and wanted to accommodate us as best as possible he must have showed me atleast 10 different room suites but they all had the same musty mold smell. I indicated to Max that all the rooms have the a/c turned off apparently to save on energy cost but if the room is unoccupied for a time it can cause for development of mold. Most high end hotels leave the rooms with a/c on constantly to avoid this problem and maintain furniture, textiles, bedding, walls from mold. We were exhausted and about to just checkout but Max knew it was late and just wanted for us to be able to rest. He showed me what looked to be the presidential suite it apparently didnt have the odor the other rooms had ( maybe because the a/c was kept on in this room or turned on in advance). The only problem was that it only had one bed but I just wanted my mother to be able to rest and I agreed to sleep on a roll-in twin size bed . Max was great he did everything possible to accommodate us but the rooms I have to say has seen better days. We decided to check out the following morning and Max had already informed Sylvia the day shift manager of the situation and we were not charged for the night. Sylvia was very helpful and had the hotel driver take us to another hotel of our choosing. I give the staff a 5 star but the rooms do not live up to a high end  establishment it claims  to be I can only give it 1 star as mold is a very serious health issue. My mother has stayed in this hotel about 2 times previous  times to this and enjoyed those stays very much and was actually looking forward to it but this time it was just disappointing.

Overall service is decent.
Especially the staff help me to take photos in front of the gate with my car. That was really a good part of this trip. All of my friends said the pic is superb.

The inner part of this hotel is luxurious when it's with designed style in dark colors. I like it. Thanks.

Booked this room for my family travel because Chilin Lin got married here haha. Glad that I chose here. Great details from pillow to mattress to face mask to snack&drinking bar. I really enjoyed staying here. Will book again if I visit Tainan again.

reviews.text:
The B&B "Guangfa Residence" in downtown Tainan, where I stayed on this business trip, has a diverse array of businesses on the first floor: a coffee shop, a wig shop, and a bar called BAR MIU. After 9:00 PM, they offered a soft opening for a tipple, with complimentary welcome cocktails 🍹. The cocktails were sour and sweet (based on white wine with a hint of plum wine), and were delicious.

The room's furnishings are simple and understated. The two large closets resemble an ordinary bedroom. The exposed concrete walls and high-legged table lend a modern touch. The double bed 🛏️ is topped with a small round table. It's a shame the potted greenery 🪴 by the window is plastic; otherwise, a short nap in the slanting afternoon light would be so relaxing.

This B&B, which opened at the end of 2023, formerly housed a local department store. The original site was demolished and rebuilt over seven years, reflecting the owner's deep remembrance of his elders. FAAA Coffee on the first floor also serves as the B&B's check-in desk. It closes at 6:00 PM and check-in is available until 7:30 PM.

The second floor is a common area, offering drip coffee, a refrigerator, and a water dispenser. After 9:00 PM, the adjacent bar, BAR MIU, offers a welcome drink.

The surrounding area is well-equipped with amenities, and the popular dining and entertainment districts of Guohua Street and Hai'an Road are nearby. This stylish and sophisticated guesthouse is a must-see for those who enjoy an industrial feel.

I love this Tainan B&B! The location is super convenient, less than a ten-minute drive from the station and close to the Anping coastline!
Guohua Street is a one-minute walk away, making it super convenient for snacks. 😚
The first floor houses a cafe and bar, which has a great atmosphere. The overall architecture is beautiful, and the gray concrete has a very classy feel.

The B&B's housekeepers are also fantastic! They're always responsive to any questions. If you extend your stay, they'll even help with cleaning and tidying up. Although it's in a busy area, it's very quiet at night. There's a bathtub for soaking in, and Netflix is ​​available. It's simply perfect. 😍
Love it! I'll definitely be back!

As soon as we stepped through the door, we were pleasantly surprised by the rich aroma of coffee, and the entire space was filled with a warm and relaxing atmosphere. The service from the front desk staff was impeccable—friendly and attentive. They not only proactively upgraded our room but also took extra care when my girlfriend was feeling unwell and in tears. They not only patiently inquired about her condition but also quickly helped find a nearby gastroenterology clinic. These thoughtful gestures truly warmed my heart.

Furthermore, from the amenities to the hardware, every detail was exquisitely crafted, with attention to detail and a truly satisfying experience. This stay far exceeded our expectations and made us want to return to Tainan just for this hotel. Highly recommended to anyone seeking a hotel that combines quality and warmth! (It's also close to popular attractions.)

The bathroom sink was small, the hair dryer was weak, and you had to take off your shoes and change into slippers on the first floor, which was a bit inconvenient.

The decor was clean, beautiful, and simple. The elevator was a bit slow, so if there were multiple groups of guests, the wait was long. The stairwell was not air-conditioned and was quite hot and stuffy.

Check-out was at 11:00. I realized I had forgotten to bring tofu, so they rented some at the front desk. The service was excellent, and communication was conducted via Line.

The last picture shows the welcome cocktails you could redeem at the bar next door with your room card. They were white wine, plum wine, and apple juice (if I remember correctly). They were not overly alcoholic, but rather sweet.

This stay was truly wonderful!
From the hotel's amenities to the attentive service, everything was truly amazing!

A special thank you to the staff for noticing we were feeling unwell and for proactively checking in and helping us find nearby clinics. That moment of care was so heartwarming, I almost cried (; ;)
Even better, they even upgraded our room for free, making our entire trip even more perfect.
Thank you for your thoughtfulness. I'll definitely be back when I'm in Tainan!

reviews.text:
Decent size rooms and beds weren't bad. Has a coffee, tea, and dessert area where you can sit in the afternoons. It is not inconveniently located but not very close to sites and interesting areas.

Maple Hotel in Tainan offers a comfortable and affordable stay, perfect for both business and leisure travelers. Located in the city center, it provides easy access to major attractions, shopping areas, and public transportation, making it an ideal base for exploring the city. The hotel features modern, well-designed rooms that are clean and well-maintained, with comfortable beds and necessary amenities like free Wi-Fi, air conditioning, and flat-screen TVs.

Guests often highlight the hotel’s quiet atmosphere, making it a great choice for those looking for a peaceful retreat. The staff is friendly and attentive, always willing to assist with any requests or provide recommendations for local dining and attractions. Additionally, the hotel offers a simple breakfast buffet, which is a convenient option for guests starting their day.

While Maple Hotel may not offer the luxury of larger, high-end hotels, it provides excellent value for money. The facilities are basic but functional, and the rooms are a good size, ensuring a pleasant stay. Some guests have mentioned that the hotel could benefit from more variety in its breakfast options, but overall, it’s a solid choice for travelers looking for a clean, comfortable, and well-located hotel in Tainan.

Hotel is relatively old. Rather quaint.
Plus points: Bathroom is big, ample space; bed (king sized) is big; shower water pressure is good. There's a kettle in the room.

Not so great: bathroom has no mirrors; no safe in room; pillow way too soft and flat; duvet couldn't cover whole bed; cupboard has only 2 hangers; wifi unsecured and slow, keeps dropping; water takes way too long to get hot, waste of water.
Overall a not too bad but maybe look into the details.

The female receptionists are not friendly. The hotel claims to have Wi-Fi, but it doesn’t work at all. The room is very old, and the laundry service is not available within the hotel, making it very inconvenient. I would not recommend this hotel to my friends or relatives if they are visiting Tainan.

Our stay didnt started well: Awful service from the 2 people at the front desk, not welcoming and it was not even busy. The morning : the 2 girls were nice though, probably because we were already clients.

No wifi with code: hard to connect and stay connected. If you need to work: its a big NO go.

Glad our room was kinda great (except the hard matress), it was spatial, easy to park in the garage under the hotel & free bike to ride around town.
Cozy place, decent price. Good job. You can get a free snack in the first floor.

reviews.text: My 3rd times here! Highly recommended to anyone who wants to stay in a boutique hotel! Make sure have their signature breakfast (a la carte style)!

The highlight for me was the 5 to 6pm “wine hour” where basically they have free flow on the floor - they put the bottles there and in case you need a refill just call the receptionist. During our stay they provided sake on our floor for both pf the nights.

Rooms: they are small but I found the mattress and pillows to be very good for me.
Toilet is great too with hi-tech toilet seat.

Some reviews are talking about hearing the neighbours, we didn’t have this problem. Our room was facing the back of the building abd it was extremely quiet (not sure if it’s the same for the main road facing rooms).

Location: quite centrally positioned but a 10-15 min walk to a MRT station.

No facilities like gym or swimming pool.

We didn’t eat at their famous restaurant this time.

All in all this has been a great hotel and I would definitely return. Book in advance for better prices.

My one-night stay at the Musa Hotel was a truly enjoyable experience.

What I loved:
* The convenience of having a Michelin-starred restaurant on the lower floor for breakfast was a fantastic start to the day.
* The hotel's decor struck a perfect balance of understated modern elegance and cleanliness, with the room featuring beautiful wooden flooring, excellent natural light, and a comfortable bed.
* The unique concept of different wine-themed collaborations on each floor added a special touch to my stay. Daily Happy Hour (5:00 PM-6:00 PM) allowed us to savor limited-edition wines from these themed wineries.
* The rooftop bar had a relaxed atmosphere, and the service was exceptional.
What I didn't love:
* Unfortunately, the soundproofing in the room was lacking, and I could hear the crying of the kid next door, which was quite bothersome.

Overall, Musa Hotel offers one of the best staycation experiences in Taipei, making it a definite recommendation for couples seeking a short, relaxing escape.

When planning for my trip to Taipei after more than 3 years a hiatus of traveling, this hotel did draw my attentions was the wine and dine. I arrived the hotel in the early afternoon, the staff let me to do the check-in procedure first. It was fast and smooth. Since the room wasn’t ready, I just left my luggage at the concierge. I stepped out to have a coffee and snack. My room was ready when I came back to the hotel 90 minutes later and my luggage had already delivered there.

I booked a Urban Deluxe Room with City view. Room was very clean and bright with decent size. The amenities are very nice. The closet located at the entrance but also be able to access from the bathroom, so it was very convenient to get ready in the morning. The bed was very comfy!

One of the highlights of this hotel is the free “Wine O’clock” from 17:00-18:00 at the Super Bar of each floor, also snacks bar with all sort of candy bars, sweets, cookies, coffee, tea and bottle water…were available 24 hours. Guest can enjoy the fine wines from 7 super wineries from 6 countries. Unfortunately I didn’t make the reservation with their Michelin 2 star restaurant Molina de Urdániz which is the big highlight of Hotel Mvsa!

Staff are very polite and friendly! I didn’t hear too much of the noises from street even though it’s next to highway. Overall, my stay was very enjoyable! Definitely it’s highly recommended to any people into wine and dine!

I had a wonderful surprised with the upgrade to Winery Deluxe Room during my stay. Room was very spacious with a long window bench and a deep soaking bath tub, separate shower & Japanese smart toilet. A large wardrobe with safety box was placed  right next to the entrance. Bed was large queen size bed.

The best part of my stay is the breakfast. I tried three main dishes and the are all good.
Few suggestions:
1. Restaurant staff should not keep touching their masks (one person did it very often during my breakfast & lunch); 2. All drinks in the room are too sweet. I need low sugar content soft drinks; 3. Need to response email or LINE faster ( under staff, I think); 4. The meat dishes of lunch menu is under salt

reviews.text: The location of this place is excellent. It manages to maintain a quiet atmosphere despite being in a busy area. It's not far from the Civic Square and the adjacent pedestrian street, yet the rooms are very quiet. The room isn't large, but I really like the hair dryer here. Usually, the hair dryers in hotels don't have much power, but this one is great. There is a small issue though. There's always a smell of paint wafting into my room. I'm not sure if it's from a new installation or fresh paint somewhere. If you're traveling with kids, it might be a good idea to check with the front desk. Since I'm only staying for two days, I didn't dwell on it too much and didn't ask to change rooms. That's about it. Looking forward to the next time.

The hotel is situated in a part of the city which is choc-a-bloc with both shopping and eating outlets. It is also
across from a pedestrianised area which turned into a vibrant area on Friday as families and young couples came out to take part in  the Christmas festivities.
The rooms are nice but have some quirks such as no drinking water in the room but has to be fetched from a water cooler. There was teaching and coffee but no milk and sugar, and no spoons to stir either. The bathrooms have some basic amenities like shampoo and a basic toiletries kit but spending from 2025, those have to be purchased as new government regulations on conservation kick in.
The breakfast was really good, especially the variety of dumplings on offer for breakfast.
Staying there due to a 2-night business trip. The room really shows the history, but still comfy enough. It is quite nice that some floors have free sparkling water dispensers.

Rooms appeared clean, but the overall atmosphere was stifling. It reeks of decades old furniture with a musty odor. 1 of the toilet doors cannot be closed fully as the hinge was off. Toilet was quite clean, but you can definitely feel the age as everything was yellowed out. One good thing was the huge and spacious room.

Parking was difficult to find initially, and there wasn't any staff around to guide us into the hotel parking lot. Someone from our car had to get down and rush to ask the counter the location of the carpark.

The breakfast buffet was a standard Chinese spread, but it wasn't very spectacular. The gym was downgraded to a single room with very limited equipment.

I will not recommend this hotel to anyone, due to its aging facilities and rooms.
Room is clean. Service is excellent. (The person at the door could called the cab for you.) Central to every place that's interesting. I will definitely coming back.

The room are too old n not clean as there are Spider web on the wall and Ceiling.

I only booked this hotel because it was close to the doctor’s office where I was having my medical procedure. The price I paid for the room was not worth it in my opinion. The curtain was ripped. There were cobwebs hanging off the ceiling. The towels were thin and flailing at the ends. There was severe mildew on the bath stool. There was no hand soap at the sink. I knew they didn’t provide personal hygiene products when I booked the room but I didn’t expect having to bring my own hand soap. I had to use my face wash every time I want to wash my hands so I don’t have to go back and forth to the shower to pump the soap from the dispenser. I don’t know if it’s the company trying to save money masking under saving the environment or a housing keeping issue but a better jobs needs to done. There were also holes in the sheets, a dark stain on one of the pillows and the comforter smelled.

I was able to get a decent sleep the first night without earplugs because there was minimal noise but there was constant door slamming, people talking throughout the next day/night that I had to wear earplugs to get any sleep at night.

I went downstairs to the receptions desk and asked for some toilet paper and was told house keeping would refill it if it runs low. I advised her I didn’t opt for housekeeping. When she came back
she advised there is also extras in the drawer. Would I have come all the way down from my work if I haven’t checked the entire room??

Suffice to say, I will not be staying here again next time I’m in town because this stay was more than enough.

Great breakfast, comfortable rooms. Affordable prices.

reviews.text:
My mother stayed at this hotel for 5 nights. The full amount for the stay was paid in cash after check-in.

On the plus side, the location is unbeatable, close to the Maple Garden and the expensive Qi-qi area.

Unfortunately, the stay was plagued by some serious problems. The room wasn't in the best condition, as you can see from the pictures, it was very humid, and even the air conditioning didn't help. So I brought my own Panasonic dehumidifier to make the room comfortable to sleep in and get the humidity below 60%.

The biggest problem was that after two nights there was a power cut and the hotel staff turned on some diesel generators in the basement. The worst part was that the carbon monoxide from these generators went up to the second floor and filled the air in the corridor. I got a call from my mum that her room was starting to smell like smoke. My girlfriend and I had to come late in the evening to assess the situation and speak to the management. The receptionist was nice and respectful, but there was nothing she could do about the situation. So we all went up the stairs to the room and had to turn back because of the thick smoke, even the receptionist could not breathe properly. We then tried to find a solution, but turning off the generators was not an option, nor was getting another room as the hotel was apparently fully booked. Basically there was nothing the hotel could do, just let it be, I was shocked. My mum could not stay and sleep in a state like that, with her room filled with smoke, so we took her home and asked for a refund for this crazy trouble. The next day a manager said we could only get 1500NT$ off as compensation but my mum paid more than 12,500NT$ for the whole stay and the manager refused to cancel the other nights or give any more refund.

Because of this terrible customer service we have just booked another hotel (Marriot Fairfield) and will never return to this place. The fear of carbon monoxide poisoning while sleeping is a life threatening situation and absolutely unacceptable and should not be ignored by hotel management.

Comfortable rooms with a good Asian style breakfast buffet in the morning. Our van was too big for the garage, but they provided complimentary parking at a lot nearby. The hotel is about a 10 minute walk to a night market.
Been here again and again since years ago, lovely staff, amazing location, cozy rooms!

reviews.text: Best place to stay! People here are way to nice, very clean, very comfortable. We loved it! Look for Lala Yin, she's the best!

Location:
I wanted a hotel where I could nap at any time without hearing the hustle and bustle of city life. This place fits the bill perfectly—it’s not next to an MRT station or a night market, so it’s quiet.

A bus stop just a minute away connects you to the MRT and the rest of Kaohsiung with no more than one transfer.

The area feels very safe, with two police stations within a 5-minute walk.

PX Mart is also 5 minutes away for any essentials or forgotten items.

The LRT to Dream Mall and also both Gushan Ferrys are easily accessible.

Google Maps shows plenty of public transit options, and Uber wait times are consistently under 5 minutes.

Amenities:
This is the kind of hotel that doesn’t nickel-and-dime you.

Complimentary bottled water (and sometimes tea and drinks at the front desk) is a nice touch.

The bidet with a heated seat was a must-have—and they delivered.

The basic gym has four types of cardio machines and a weight pulley system up to 150+ lbs.

On the rooftop, there are coin-operated washers, a detergent dispenser, and dryers, with clear instructions in both English and Chinese.

Breakfast options include both buffet and personalized meals, and the staff even customized a very specific health-conscious, religious-friendly meal for us.

Service:
Outstanding. The staff are multilingual, always warm, and extremely accommodating. They went above and beyond—whether it was adjusting meals for the pickiest eater or honoring eco-friendly room cleaning requests. They even kept a full notepad of our very specific preferences and still served us with a smile.

TL;DR: Exceptional service, quiet location, thoughtful amenities. I’d definitely stay here again.

A decent hotel. One confusing policy -
The gym opens only at 10:00, but breakfast is served 7:00-9:30. And checkout is at 11:00… which makes the gym practically useless. I tried to ask them to open it earlier, but in a typical Chinese style, they are extremely inflexible.

It is clean and quiet hotel with comfortable rooms and very kind team at the reception desk. Localisation is approx 20 minuts walk to the metro station. District was not super elegant, but I felt safe in streets.

This is my 2nd time staying at Kaohsiung A Hotel and so fortunate that I got a big room in the corner... It has bath tub which I need to make my body relax. Since it is in the corner, of course the space is big and no doubt for it cleanliness. The staff were helpful with my requests. Breakfast is OK, a lot of things to be chosen. The area is not a busy area but for me is ok, since I have busy day time. So, I need to rest at night... They have coffee shop in lobby area which I didnt have time to try... Hopefully when I go to Kaoshiung again and will stay here again, I will try their coffee...

reviews.text: Location was amazing very close to all our activities. We enjoyed our stay so much. The rooms were very clean and very spacious. Even just a standard room had a lot of room and the shower was amazing. Literally no complaint about this place at all as it was everything we were looking for. The rooms look just like the pictures

Cheap. Not the best but great for value. Includes breakfast. Quite dusty. It wasn't noisy while we were there. Parking was a bit confusing but figured it out. Bed was comfy. Shower was hot so that's good. It does suddenly get a bit hotter at times but still it was good. Wasn't a lot of food choices but maybe because we got here about 8pm.

After reading the reviews, booking a room, and staying here, I feel like I am definitely the minority in terms of opinion and feel compelled to share. First of all, the cleanliness left much to be desired. The shower was not cleaned well and there were stray hairs left in both the shower and bathroom.

My main complaint however has to do with the room layout. For whatever reason, the toilet and shower were housed in separate "booths" that were not completely walled off from the main room. Both of these booths were small, and the main room itself was small. This may be fine if you are staying here with a partner, but for anyone else it makes things extremely awkward. There's no "bathroom" to change in – you have to change in the shower and hope that your dry clothes don't get wet. Also, don't stay here if you don't want to hear your roommate's every start farts and pee streams all throughout the night. It is just too loud and disruptive.

Finally, the hotel for some reason only provided one small towel and one large towel per person. I was staying with two other people and when I asked for more towels, they said they were only able to provide two more. I've never seen a hotel with so few towels available.

Q21 Hotel located at a good area with many Taiwan tradition food and landmarks. The hotel itself is tidy, with new and trendy interior design. The front desk is helpful as well. Overall, I feel good staying here. One thing to note is that there is no closet in the room I selected, but then the room is large enough for me to open both of my suitcases. Which is fine and good as I am not staying long, but this could be a draw back for you.

Came on a Thursday afternoon at 12.30pm - not crowded at all

Food was interesting! Worth a try if you’re in Tainan

With a tour group. Walking in from the main door, you will be treated with a grand entrance of the oriental dinning hall view. So the more popular dishes are generally served to the tourists. Had their signature Egg Noodle (蛋蛋面). Silky egg noodle with Clear soup. For a Singaporean like me, Fish porridge is good. 清淡。meat balls are tasty. First serving is the cold dish. A very local dining restaurant. The egg noodle is a must try. I believe they should have very good dishes for dinner. Yes, highly recommended. 👍🏻👍🏻👍🏻

Highly recommended if you want to try out all the traditional Tainan deli in one place.
Fresh ingredients and friendly service.

The food tastes much more better than I thought, do try out the Dan Zai Noodle, tofu pudding, as well as the set menu here ( best for group of 2-3 people )

Expect some of the local dishes does not match your taste bud, for example the thick soup is too sweet for me, but overall I think it’s a pleasant dining experience.

Would definitely come back for more :)

reviews.text:
Our friends took us to this local beef hotpot restaurant for dinner, it’s quite a unique dining experience. Food was good and the beers and wines are very reasonably priced, selection was also better than expected. However, we saw a few big “insects” that really bothered us.

It’s famous for the hand sliced local beef, which is fresh and not been frozen. The hotpot had lots of miscellaneous ingredients inside, and lots more you can order more from the menu. And there are lots of sauces, ginger slices and vinegar you can mix for your own taste, I like the spicy fermented bean paste, while there are other simple choices like soy sauce or you can also eat it without.

Atmosphere is good and a wide variety of food to choose from. Hotpot is the popular selection, can order some local dishes as well. Call to reserve table in advance as there is always a waiting queue.
Very recommended dining place in Tainan!!

The restaurant is spacious and cozy. The owner is very enthusiastic and kind. There is usually very crowded but the food is served very quickly. Fresh local food and fill your hunger pangs. The location is easy to find and has convenient parking. Highly recommended.

I visited this restaurant every time I came to Tainan. Comfortable seats. Air-conditioned. Delicious fresh beef hotpot. Pork (梅肉) and squid meatballs are also recommended. The aged steak is surprisingly good with the hotpot. The cold-brewed tea is a good pairing with the food. Crafted beer is available as well. A restaurant suitable for family and friend gatherings. Price is reasonable.

This is one of the more famous hot pot places in Tainan, and it didn't disappoint. The soup is amazing! We also ordered the giant grilled prawns which were cooked perfectly. They bottle their own tea, we got two different bottles and I think they were quite good. Good place for group. The staffs were extremely friendly and accommodating as we had two young kids with us.

reviews.text:
A friend recommended this well known traditional Taiwanese restaurant.

Food: 4/5 - we enjoyed the steamed fresh prawns and chicken herbal soup. I was disappointed with the steamed mud crab with sticky rice. The crab was small and didn’t have much meat for that particular crab. The herbal soup was flavorful and tasty. Something my mom used to make.

Service: 3/5 - lots of servers standing around but not as attentive. We had a bottle of sake & ended up serving ourselves.

Atmosphere: 4/5 - bright and clean inside. They had fresh Easter lilies in vases. If you don’t like the scent as is, it may affect your meal.

This is a very famous restaurant in Tainan city where you can get the traditional banquet dishes in the old times.
The price is reasonable, dishes are yummy, service is quite prompt.
We ordered almost all the signature dishes, in the end, the restaurant offers free dishes of fruit and desserts, very sweet.

This place is very famous for their crab with sticky rice but I am very disappointed. We ordered takeout because we don’t have reservation and it’s possible we had different quality of food. we waited for about 15 minutes for our food, in my experience it takes more than 15 minutes to cook the rice. I am fairly certain the rice is precooked separately not together with the crab.
And the rice is soggy, it does not have the right chew you expect from sticky rice. The quality of this dish definitely does not match the hype and the price they charge. Not recommended!!

The stars are given based on this single trip.
The service was pretty good for sure. I didn’t make an early reservation, but they managed to squeeze a table for me. I really appreciated them.
The dishes were awesome even though I didn’t get to try their signature. The only thing I can be picky about is the soup. It was too sweet. Oh, and it would be nice if the yummy fried rice was a bit more.

Very well known for traditional Taiwanese cuisine.  The restaurant itself is a piece of history.

Food is quite good with the set menu catered to smaller groups of people who also wish to try most of their famous dishes. However, I would still suggest go with a big group of people and order their signature dishes in big servings to get the maximum traditional Taiwanese banquet experience.

A very good place to introduce Taiwanese cooking/culture to foreigners

reviews.text: A bit of a long line, but not unbearable to wait through since it moves pretty fast. You fill out your order sheet beforehand, so they get your food out pretty fast once you sit down. We got the beef noodle soup, some stir fried vegetables, beef brisket soup, and some stir fried noodles. Definitely better than the place we went to the other day, the broth was extremely flavorful with hand-cut noodles that really soaked in that delicious broth.

The beef soup is heavenly and full of pure beefy flavor without those unnecessary condiments or spices you get elsewhere. Options to eat in air conditioned room. Must come early else you need to wait in line. The beef slices are tender and delicious.

Since 1968, this beloved eatery has been serving up mouthwatering hand-sliced beef, lightly cooked in a rich, bubbling broth made from beef bones and veggies. The tender slices are best enjoyed dipped in their signature sweet, thick soy sauce with a touch of shredded ginger—simple, comforting, and absolutely delicious!

This spot serves the best beef soup in the area, hands down. A Tainan specialty, it’s an absolute must-try if you’re visiting. You’ll queue up to order and pay before grabbing a seat, and while the prices are a bit high for a street-side restaurant, the generous portions and incredible flavor make it worth every dollar.

The food comes out quickly, the service is solid, and their popularity speaks for itself—they’ve even opened a second location within walking distance if the line for this location gets too long. I highly recommend the premium cut beef soup, beef fried rice, and beef tongue side. Just thinking about it has me drooling. This is a must-visit!

Started queuing up at 11.45 there was already a long queue. Waited for an hour and a half in sun. The meat arrived at the shop at 12.03 so it’s very fresh. Our beef soup was delicious, the beef was soft and the soup was sweet (not sugar sweet but vegetable/ meat soup).

I've been coming here since I was a kid. Food is always delicious no matter what you choose. Bur if I had to choose, definitely pick the Xiao Long Bao and the Original Beef Noodle Soup. They are top-tier dishes here. They get busy very fast, so it's best to go when they open, at 11am.

P.S. They have unlimited soy milk!!

The service is fast. Food is very filling and delicious. Ambiance is very vibrant. Overall, eating here is a very good experience to enjoy and taste Taiwanese food.

I really like their xiao long bao, jiaozi, yellow bun, and unlimited tea and milk. 🥰

Edit: I updated this to remind myself that my favorite noodles here is the one with mustard.

First visit to this place and i have to give credit to the bowl of noodle ive ordered. Broth is so flavourful and the noodle was so chewy.

Had a basket of their fresh prawn dumpling. Although there wasnt much soup in the dumpling but the meat was so tasty!

For this amount of food, i suppose the price is reasonable.

Really good affordable food - dumplings, dim sum and scallion pancake. The chicken roll is the best. They offer free black tea or soy milk. It’s always busy, but the queue goes quickly. Very popular with the locals, you can’t go wrong here. Check it out.
Food tastes good - guotie, hakao, spareribs, chaoso and spring rolls (unfortunately they do not make these anymore) .

reviews.text:
At 600nt/person you would expect a bit more in terms of service and food quality.  No napkins, just little tissues you’d get at a noodle shop.  The service staff are attentive and friendly, definitely a highlight.  The food was hit or miss: set meal salad came drenched in blue berry yoghurt covering the top, felt a bit like an afterthought but was still good.  The soup was tasty but we thought it was a bit sweet. The real disappointments were the pasta dishes, pasta was overcooked and swimming in sauce, chefs seemed to have taken too many artistic liberties.  The dessert brownie was basic but definitely saved the day and removed the depression caused by the pasta.  The extra order of potatoes appetizer was also memorably good, especially when compared to their pasta.
Can’t say we would want to be back again, as there are better choices at this price point.  Rather disappointing when you factor in the framed Cordon Bleu certifications hanging on the wall behind the cashier.

Cute building though, might just be better to enjoy the view from outside.
We tried the mushroom risotto and shrimp pasta and truffle potatoes. The mushroom risotto was best. Great service by the staff! Thank you.
Good place with good dish for sure. I do believe it can be better if the ribeye steak can be richer.
Hidden gem in the alleys of Tainan. I especially liked the potato dish. It was perfectly cooked, coupled with truffles...yum.

reviews.text: First time dining in this restaurant. We are from Singapore, there for visiting. We were there last Friday and was invited by our ex CEO to this very fine dining place with delicious appetisers, soup, main, dessert and drinks. We brought our kids there too. The food is nice, the environment is wonderful and the service there was awesome. The staff is sweet and friendly as well. Strongly recommend a must visit for locals and tourists. The location is easy to find. The price is reasonable.
Friends and I went for a Sunday lunch and had a delicious and varied set of dishes, all of them well worth trying. We really enjoy its cosy atmosphere and decorations.  Definitely recommended 👌

This is a gorgeous restaurant with amazing food and impressive service. We tried the Surf and Turf and it was delicious. The lobster 🦞 was tender, succulent and full of taste. The Ribeye steak 🥩 was excellent. French 🇫🇷 onion soup was piping hot and authentic. Parma Ham and melon also perfect. Overall it was a great dining experience. I recommend you try this restaurant if you visit Tainan.  The prices are on the high side for Taiwan 🇹🇼

Restaurant looks like a high class restaurant but waiters look like busy about something else. We request change table because we have reservations for window table. They give us a table which faces a wall outside.
Sounds funny and they ask us to explain to get the right table for our table when we make our reservation.
We make reservations and request for a window table which means we want to look outside not to face a wall outside.
It’s my birthday but same desert as my friend. Only has a candle on top my desert.
Waiters are not friendly when we want to change table even at the end we didn’t find any one come for table. It’s too weird.

All our steaks were cooked perfectly medium rare. The grilled pork chops were amazing, it was one of the best things I ate on that trip. My sister loved the lamb chops with mint sauce.  Overall the food was excellent! Looking forward to eating here again when we visit Tainan.

Tainan food at its best... don’t just do the street food. This restaurant is the local’s go to restaurants for all big and small special occasions.

Not the best start when service here is condescending when you aren't ordering enough. Flavor wise, most dishes are bland and do not feel special. The most tasty to our group was the fried shrimp appetizer and the desert soup. The eel, crab, and fried rice are passable at best.

This is a branch of the famous old Taiwanese restaurant in Tainan in the mall! The restaurant is splendid and its courses are special. Those who would like to taste the authentic and typical local food should come here to enjoy a scrumptious meal!

reviews.text:
Food is good. It is definitely worth a visit. The texture of shrimp rolls is great. You can taste chunks of shrimps that's been hand chopped rather than shredded in a big mixer. They serve garlic with your order, and it does help to wash a way some of the oily ness when you are eating deep fried food.
I just wish that they could serve beers to wash away the oily ness, but the only serve slightly sugared black tea for beverage.
I think one set of shrimps and fish cake is enough for a grown up. The dry rice noodles is ok.
I don't know if they provide a English meny, since I use a translator app to translate the order ticket. I recommend this place.

I am not sure if we didn't order the right stuff or if this place is just over rated. The food was ok. But not worth the hype. Try if it you are in the area but don't make a trip for it. Shrimp rolls were best thing. Braised pork also good. But everything else was just mid. The thick fish soup was interesting. Very fishy. The prok w rice was also good. Probably 2nd best. No beer but you can go next door and buy. Or if you have good stuff bring your own.

When you visit Anping, this restaurant is highly recommended since it serves local delicious dishes in Tainan. It serves famous shrimp rolls, milk fish congee, milk fish sausages, braised pork rice, and other various seafood dishes. Gourmets are advised to come here if they intend to experience the charming  local culture and cuisine in Tainan. Pay a visit. Ha....

Famous for their deep fried prawn rolls but what I really enjoyed here was the 虱目鱼 Milk Fish Skin. So far the fish skin I've tried is usually deep fried, but this is not. It's like boiled/steamed and drizzled with their homemade braised minced pork. Something truly unique I've not tried anywhere else. The fried rolls were really good too, 真材实料, even the seafood cake, was filled with chunky bits of prawn and squid, not just seafood-flavoured flour paste.

reviews.text: It was my first visit, and the food was excellent. They open at 4 AM, so you can grab a late-night snack or breakfast! Their menu focuses on fresh, plump fish, with a sweet, non-greasy broth. The braised pork rice is juicy, and they also offer a fragrant, chewy braised egg and seafood congee with a variety of toppings. One bite and you'll be hooked! Friendly staff, definitely worth a try!

It’s totally my kind of breakfast since I’m more into rice than flour-based dishes. The congee is light but full of flavor, with fresh seafood like milkfish and oysters. It feels simple, comforting, and very local. The place looks low key, but you can tell it’s a favorite among locals. A perfect way to start the day in Tainan.
The congee is OK, cannot match the Cantonese style. The rice dumpling is covered with minced meat sauce.

We ate here twice because it’s THAT good! We even skipped our hotel breakfast so that we could eat it a second time.

Tried the fish skin porridge, which still came with a fair bit of meat, and also the fish belly and oyster porridge. Both were really really yummy. The fish was completely deboned and not at all fishy. Oysters were also very fresh. It might look simple but I think this qualifies as one of the best meals I had in Tainan.

Milkfish porridge is best served in this small breakfast restaurant. It continues to serve until porridge out of stock. A lot of morning transient traffic plus irregular business hours which are based on lunar calendar to be minded if you decide to give a try. Otherwise, a very tasty, typical Tainan breakfast eating style you don’t want to miss.

I had ordered Milkfish Porridge and Braised Pork Belly over Rice. Recommended combination.

Milkfish Porridge has milkfish meat, oyster, diced celery, fried garlic, and rice.

And their curry was so fragrant that me and my partner finished every bits and pieces, leaving no speck of food behind. :) definitely recommended if you are visiting Tainan, Taipei

Must try.

as a long-stay in Taipei person, the price still too expensive for us.

Hot pot restaurant inside a renovated Taiwanese vintage house. Yuzu flavoured hot pot is served here. Choose the main courses from the menu: beef, pork, chicken and sea food platter are served here. Vegetarian hot pot is also available. The soup is clear and I like the flavour, and the meat is fresh. But I think the staff should put more of their efforts on the dining environment;  there are ants on our table and walls around us, and there is a hair on the vegetable platter the served to us🙄. The chair is not comfortable, either. Reservation is recommended, and you could request a table for a better dining experience. We three were arranged to a side table, where it isn’t proper for us to talk to each other.

I got the tomato soup base and really impressed with the flavor. The veggie and meat quality are really fresh too! Highly recommended! The only thing is the short staffed. Nice service but need more staff.

We had their famous shrimp omelet and rice with crab. Both were fantastic! We were beyond delighted with the experience and paid 880 dollars for both. They also offered complimentary tea and some delicious watermelon at the end. We're lucky to have eaten their great food Highly recommended!!

Honestly, they should be a good place to eat with great dishes, IF over half their menu wasn't items you had to reserve ahead. Should just not take walks-ins if that's the case, ended up having to choose between just a few items. Really a restaurant for big groups with plans many days ahead. The food I did get to have was great though

Went here on a Tuesday around 11:45 AM alone, not knowing it was a family-style restaurant. It wasn't busy at all, and they were able to accommodate me with a smile. All of the staff were so friendly and patient, and the food was delicious!

I ordered the shrimp pancake and the shrimp rolls. The pancake was amazing, and the shrimp rolls were tasty but didn't seem to be anything special even though it was my first time eating them.

Several times while I was eating, the staff exchanged a few words with me. They were genuinely interested in learning about me, where I'm from, etc. While the food was delicious, the staff really made the experience for me. Highly recommended!

Food was beyond fantastic.  You don't see this type of traditional Taiwanese cuisine very often nowadays.

The only downside is that the restaurant building is a bit old and dated.  The stairs are steep, so you will need to be careful, especially with elderly.  Would visit again and recommend.

Nice traditional spot with great food and service. We had their famous pork liver (豬肝) and fried shrimps with egg omelette, which were tasty, though a bit heavy. Their stir fried noodles (炒麵) and veggies (龍鬚菜) were really tasty too.

reviews.text:
The food tastes good, though a bit too sweet for me, and it feels a little heavy after finishing one portion. The price is affordable, and the eel is fresh.

The restaurant is very crowded, during dinner time you may need to wait around 20-30 minutes for a table. However, once seated, the food arrives very quickly. The staff are also friendly and helpful.

I'm on a business trip to Tainan and tried the local specialty, eel noodles. The ambiance of this restaurant isn't great, but the flavor is exceptional. The seasoning is well-balanced, with the eel being refreshingly crisp and delicious. The pork kidney soup is also rich and flavorful, making one's mouth water. Unfortunately, parking nearby is a little bit difficult and there's no option to adjust the spiciness. Although the eel noodles include peas and fresh onions, the addition of fresh chili peppers could elevate the dish to a new level.

In Tainan, a city celebrated for its culinary heritage, Eastern Castle Noodle stands out with its iconic stir-fried eel noodles. This isn’t just a dish; it’s a Tainan institution. The “wok hei”—the prized, smoky essence from a searing hot wok—is immediately apparent, with the aroma of the flash-fried noodles hitting you first.
The eel itself is the star—tender yet firm, coated in a savory, slightly sweet glaze that perfectly complements its delicate flavor. Sautéed with crisp snow peas, onions, and scallions, the textures are a delightful contrast. Each bite offers a harmonious blend of smoky noodles, rich eel, and fresh vegetables, making it an essential Tainan experience.
Experience the harmonious blend of smooth sourness and juicy eel in this dish, resulting in a perfectly balanced and truly delicious flavor.

I have visited this place at least 10 times in the last 2 weeks.
While there are plenty of excellent joints for eel noodles in Tainan, there is a handful I would consider exceptional. Depending on my mood, my favorite can change. This place comes out on top most of the time. The key to exceptional eel noodles really comes down to the following list in order:
1. freshness (that's why location matters)
2. skillz (this goes with the next one)
3. BTU (woking without the right amount of high heat to go with the skills is just a waste to the eels who gave up their lives for my belly)
4. flavor (distant 4th)

All my favorite joints in Tainan's got the first 3 locked. What sets this place apart is really the willingness to sprinkle some chili flakes in the process. It's not spicy (at least not to me), but it enhances the taste by a good magnitude.

I'd say give it a try. I highly recommend it.

reviews.text:
I am writing this review to express my heartfelt appreciation for the extraordinary dining experience my guest and I enjoyed at your esteemed restaurant on Friday night, final table of the night. It is important to mention the particularly skillful and expert meal orchestration by Chef Aaron Lee.  It was impressive how he could nod or provide a slight hand gesture and the staff would respond promptly and professionally.

The teppanyaki dinner was nothing short of perfection. Each course was presented at an impeccable pace, allowing us to savor the delightful array of delicacies. The flavors were exquisite, and it was evident that great care and creativity went into the preparation of every dish.

I would also like to commend the support staff for their impeccable service. They engaged in mindful conversations without ever interrupting our experience, striking a perfect balance between attentiveness and discretion. A special mention goes to Ella, who took extra care to explain each course in English and patiently answered all our questions. Her dedication greatly enhanced our dining experience.

The rave reviews about ROBINS at Silks Palace are indeed well-deserved. Our visit confirmed that this is a must-visit destination for anyone seeking a remarkable culinary adventure. I highly recommend making reservations to anyone who hasn't yet experienced the magic of your restaurant.

Thank you once again for providing such a memorable evening. We look forward to returning for another exceptional meal in the near future.

reviews.text: A surprising hidden gem, you’d never guess what this place is from the outside. The old house is tucked away in a narrow alley, and I had to rely on Google Maps to find it. It seems that this kind of eatery is one of the symbols of Tainan City. The place even has three adorable dogs, and their dishes are quite unique. It’s definitely a great spot for gathering with friends.

Very cozy restaurant, you feel at home with a family like environment, staffs are very friendly and nice, all furnitures are imported from Denmark, and you have some friendly dogs greeting you.
Overall the dishes are not salted, the ingredients are natural and very healthy, each dish has its own special flavor, the blueberry milkshake and the couscous salad was awesome! I had the seafood risotto and the rice was really unique, it was mixed with barley, never tried this kind of risotto. Finally the chia seed coconut pudding was also so special, it came with handmade strawberry sauce and vanilla ice cream, a combination I’d never thought of!

The meals are mainly roasted, not oiled.
Suitable for someone who looks for light meal with less calories.
Service is good , free parking with limited space, but is good enough especially in the Tainan city center.

The best restaurant I’ve visited in Taiwan.
Do not sleep on this place if you visit Tainan, the bruschetta was delicious. their hummus reminded me of home, rice was great and the beef stew was simmered to perfection. Aside from the food being amazing the atmosphere was just perfect, with incredible service, a warm welcome and best of all cute dogs walking around to make sure you have company, unless you hate dogs and nobody hates dogs don’t pass on visiting this restaurant

Probably my favorite restaurant I've been to in Tainan. Really friendly English-speaking staff (and even friendlier dogs!). The interior is beautifully designed and gives off a cozy, inviting vibe. The food is pricier than most places, but it clearly reflects the quality of the food. Would absolutely recommend this restaurant to anyone.

reviews.text: I have been here twice now and both times have been exceptional. Hopefully there is a Michelin star in their future as they deserve it. I let the staff know ahead of time that I can only speak English and they did their best to accommodate me and they provide me with a English menu. It is a quite small restaurant with only a few tables and everyone is seated and served at the same time so meals can take a while (3-4 hours). Food is delicious and the wines are pairings are nicely matched with the different courses. Will definitely be back next time I am in Tainan!

From the dining environment to the creative dishes, I had had a fantastic night at Principe!
The chef pays tribute to his root by reimagining the traditional Taiwanese cuisine with French cooking. For example, the Fricassée de poulet with French toast resembles the “coffin bread”, one of the best known street food in Tainan. Other dishes including, milkfish pie, oyster consommé and shrimp chips, also exhibit the flavours of An-Ping Old Street and An-Ping Port.
There are much more surprises that you have to experience yourself. Highly recommend ❤️

I write this as a cousin of the owner of the restaurant, Cheng Yu. Although it's easy to be biased due to the familial relations, I write this with the utmost sincerity.
I really looked forward to dining here even before they opened as Cheng Yu had shared with me that this has been a childhood dream of his and we had the opportunity to dine here as a private function with family members. Wait staff was extremely attentive, very professional in her explanations on each course and accommodating towards our needs.
I ordered the Fish whereas my husband had the Pork. The dishes were beautifully presented and tasted equally as enticing as it looked. The mushrooms on the side of the Pork was buttery and seasoned well with the Yuzu Sauce a delight to match with the Pork! Beautiful explosion of flavours!
I don't normally go for a Fish dish but I had a feeling that Principe would do an outstanding job and I wasn't wrong. The Swallowtail Fish was soft and had a lovely slightly crunchy skin and when paired with the foam, it was simply a great match. I would gladly eat this again.

Each dish was beautifully presented and the quality of the food was delicious.
It's quite obvious to me that each course had been well-contemplated and constructed. The creativity of each course as well as the play on flavours all worked very well and I liked how everything came together. It's quite clear that a lot of love and passion was put into the restaurant as a whole and not just in the food.

This will definitely not disappoint especially as Principe is such a different restaurant in Tainan. Fantastic for a special occasion or when you feel like indulging in the foodie within you!

I look forward to dining here again in future! =D
