I feel like I have to get some things off my chest.

This is my first time at this restaurant. It's actually very close to home, but I've never been there before. I thought if I get used to it, it would be on my bucket list. I knew Xuzhou cuisine is spicy and oily before I came here, so I was prepared. I parked the car but hadn't arrived yet, so my wife ordered first. We said we were dining for five people, two middle school girls and my mother. The boss recommended lamb ribs (880) and stir-fried pork intestines (small 380/large 680), and my wife ordered both. We then ordered soup: Braised Mixed Vegetables (small 380/large 680), Clay Pot Chicken (680), Shredded Potatoes (150), and Cold-mixed Preserved Eggs (200). The boss didn't ask about the size, and all the dishes served were large. After I sat down and ate, I asked the boss, and he said, "The small portion is for two people. If there are more than two people, you have to order the large portion, otherwise you won't even get a bowl of soup for each of us."

That's the problem. Even if it's for two people, shouldn't the customer decide whether to order large or small? Is it possible to order large portions without asking? Just ask, and I wouldn't be commenting here.

Later, the owner said he forgot to make the preserved egg salad, and since the four women and one man didn't eat much and were already stuffed with the other dishes, he said it wouldn't be necessary.

Conclusion:

1. The service from the hostess and waitstaff was excellent.

2. Three meats, one vegetable, and one soup cost over NT$3,000. I'll choose a different restaurant in the future.

3. Customers are given the choice of large or small portions. I don't believe that everyone with more than two people will only order the large portion.

4. When a customer asks about the size, simply saying, "Sorry I didn't ask first. I'll keep an eye on it next time." makes a huge difference.

I'm giving it three stars for the salted egg baby cabbage and shredded potatoes—they're must-orders. I didn't find the meats particularly tasty and quite expensive. Some portions are available in small and large sizes, so be sure to check. The hostess's service is excellent.

If got 0 star i will rate it as 0 star. One of the worst Taiwanese cafe/restaurant i went since a long time. First, braised pork rice is the most iconic dish to showcase Taiwan, but thats the worst braised pork rice i ever had in this place. There were no pork meat at all! 100% pork fat was served. Dare to say "Champion Braised Pork Rice"?   Should named it as Champion Braided Pork Fat Rice instead.

Second, the salted vege pork belly soup with rice. Only 3 pieces, 3 pieces, 3 pieces of meat with small size was served! With the price of RM21.90, 3 thin slice, as thin as A4 paper meat was served! Its not worth at all, the meat also look dark in colour, definitely not fresh at all.

Words for management, please check the SOP and QC the ingredients and food quality. You are well known and have lots of outlet across Malaysia, please maintain your quality!

Most disappointing was the shaved ice dessert. Very average tasting and way too sweet.

Came for lunch during Ramadan month. They have some rotating promotional set meals which is good to keep things fresh and new.
The Sauerkraut with White Pork Hotpot with shaved noodles suits my taste: Relatively light soup that's refreshingly sour but not overly so, fatty pork slices tasted amazing with the sauces provided in the set.
The Champion Braised Pork Rice is defos not for the faint of heart. Was too fatty for our taste, but it does taste great.
When asking for take-out options, the owner gave some great suggestions on certain dishes that are easier to reheat or can be eaten cold.

If ordering any of the fatty pork dishes, you may either need to have more ppl to share or try to balance it out with vege...they have sets for that too.
Tried using grab dine out and got some nice deal! Food was nice - ambience was really good with the location and service was good too…

🌟 Shin Yeh Taiwanese Cuisine – Main Restaurant (Zhongshan, Taipei)

🏆 Catchline: Flavours of Home Elevated – A Michelin-Backed Taiwanese Feast! 🇹🇼

✨ Ambience & Setting

Located in the heart of Taipei’s Zhongshan District, Shin Yeh impresses with a spacious, elegantly kept dining room that feels both refined and inviting  . With 110 tables and private rooms, it’s ideal for banquets, family gatherings, or intimate meals. The service is thoughtful—expect prompt plate changes, wet towel refreshes, and warm hospitality throughout  .

---

🍽️ Food & Signature Dishes

Scallion Oil Chicken, Pan‑Fried Pork Liver, and Fresh Almond Tofu (made by three chefs) stand out as classic hits  .

Menu balances homestyle authenticity with careful, refined execution—think rice-based dishes, comforting soups, seasonal veggies, seafood rolls, and soothing sweet-potato porridge  .

Michelin Guide inclusion is a testament to its quality and consistency  .

---

❤️ Why Locals & Chefs Choose It

Many diners point out chefs love this place—true “chef’s choice” status  .

Reviews highlight excellent soups, fresh ingredients, sturdy set‑menu options, and well‑balanced flavors  . One quoted review:

> “…The soups were so decadent and the best soups I’ve had. No matter how full I was, I couldn’t stop drinking more soup!!”

---

📊 Ratings & Accolades

Rated 4.2/5 overall—consistent praise across food quality, service, and atmosphere  .

Banquet-ready, with reservations recommended, especially on weekends  .

---

🧾 Practical Info

Feature	Details

Address	No. 34‑1 Shuangcheng Street, Zhongshan District, Taipei 10491
Hours	Lunch: 11:30–15:00 / Dinner: 17:00–21:30 daily
Ambience	Spacious interior, private rooms, cozy yet refined
Reservations	Advised for larger groups or weekend visits

---

✅ Pros & ⚠️ Cons

👍 Pros:

Authentic Taiwanese comfort food, elevated.

Ideal for groups and special occasions.

Attentive service and chef-approved reputation.

👎 Cons:

Slightly pricier than local eateries.

High-end, not street-food quirky—may feel formal for casual travellers.

---

💡 Reviewer Tips

Go for set menus to sample a wide variety of classics.

Don’t skip the soups and almond tofu—they’re crowd favourites.

Reserve in advance, especially for weekends or large parties.

---

🏁 Final Verdict

If you want a true taste of Taiwanese home cooking—done with finesse—Shin Yeh is a winner. It blends tradition with comfort, high-end service, and Michelin-level consistency. A perfect pick for celebrations, foodie explorations, or memorable meals.

I came thinking this is the Michelin-starred restaurant (Shin Yeh Taiwanese Signature), but I think it’s part of the same franchise. I ordered the set menu, and I got the standard dishes you get in Taiwanese cuisine. Fast-paced restaurant with hurrying, efficient waiters and solid food! Wished I got individual dishes though so I can try different things.

Our family came here for a birthday celebration and the food was so delicious! The set menu was so amazing with some Taiwanese dishes I’ve never tried before. They were all beautifully prepared with very fresh quality ingredients. The salad was so refreshing! The soups were so decadent and the best soups I’ve had. No matter how full I was, I couldn’t stop drinking more soup!!

The service was excellent. The servers were never far away and changed plates, provided wet hand towels throughout the meal.

Apparently, this is where chefs eat, so that says a lot!!

A Michelin star restaurant serving traditional Taiwanese cuisine. Taiwanese porridge, specifically sweet potato porridge. I think the porridge itself is a highlight, the sweet potato they use here is different, it's less fibrous, giving it a smoother texture that blends well into the porridge.

As such, most of their dishes are slightly on the saltier side, like the Deep Fried Silver Fish, Chai Po Omelette, Baby Clams marinated in Soya Sauce, Steamed Minced Meat. But they go so well with the porridge or rice.

•	Lemon green tea: overly sweet like syrup, no tea taste at all, just like lemonade.

On top of that, the bill was already overpriced, and they still charged 6% service tax + 10% service charge (16% total). Service was also unfriendly.

Honestly, the food and service quality do not justify the price at all. Definitely won’t be coming back.

TLDR: This is the Alishan coffee place that has no coffee!

(1) The door says "COFFEE: Taiwan Alishan Coffee"

(2) Promo poster on the outside along the pedestrian walkway has pictures of some drink including coffee and says in Chinese: "Buy any DRINK, add a Taiwanese Wheelcake for RM2 only"

(3) Same promo poster is placed on every table in A3.

We couldn't find coffee in the menu or in the promo. We asked the staff. Manager person told us they don't sell coffee.
Wait what?
Yes, no coffee.
We pointed to the coffee pictures and he said don't have.
Erm... Ok....
We order a Boba Soya and want to try the Wheelcake. Just add RM2, right?
Nope. That promo cannot be useful.
Wait, why not? Isn't it any drink?
No, that promo is only when you buy coffee.
Huh? Then can we order coffee?
No, they don't sell coffee.
So why did they put this promo up for?!?!?

None of the staff speaks or reads Chinese and this promo is written in Chinese so they don't understand what's written in their own promo. It's honestly frustrating.

Atmosphere ⭐⭐⭐

We had a wonderful dining experience at Shan Shin. The ambience was elegant yet comfortable, and the service from 琇庭, 宜妤, and AA was outstanding – very attentive, warm, and professional. The food was excellent. Our top highlights were:
•	Scallion Chicken (蔥油雞) – tender, juicy, and bursting with fragrance.
•	Seaweed Egg (芥菜炒蛋) – homely and flavorful, one of our favorites.
•	Braised Beef Brisket with Vegetables – rich and hearty.
•	Stir-fried Broccoli with Mushrooms – fresh and crisp.
•	Oyster Tofu – unique and delicious.
•	Steamed Fresh Fish – perfectly cooked and fresh.

We visited Shan Shin during our workshop in Taichung with a group of twelve people and had a wonderful dining experience.
Since we were twelve, we were able to try a wide variety of dishes, and everyone was fully satisfied. In particular, the Roasted Duck & Duck Bone Soup, Boiled Fish With Pickled Mustard, and Fish Maw and Crab Roe with Tofu Stew were outstanding and left a deep impression.

The manager kindly explained that some dishes may take longer to prepare, so it’s best to decide the menu in advance when making a reservation. We followed this advice and enjoyed a smooth dining experience within the 90-minute seating time.

All the staff were very kind and attentive, which made the experience even more pleasant.
One more tip: if the in-app reservation system doesn’t work, you can also make a booking via LINE chat, and the staff responds very kindly.(@922gpxxr)

Highly recommended for group dining and anyone who wants to enjoy authentic and creative Taiwanese cuisine. 🌟

At first, we were told the restaurant was full, but soon after, a kind lady came to us and let us know they had a spot available.

The atmosphere felt like a true Taiwanese family-style restaurant, with big tables and a warm, welcoming vibe. The portions were huge, incredibly flavorful, and there were so many options that I wanted to try them all. The staff were wonderful — always checking in to make sure the food was good and that everything was perfect.

We didn’t take many photos, but we enjoyed every second of our meal. It was a lovely night, and we absolutely loved this place. If we come back to Taiwan, we’ll 100% be back at Shan Shin. Keep up the great work!

reviews.text: My aunt and uncle took me to this place. We arrived before noon so we are the only guests for now. It's quiet and nice. Appetizers are very fresh. We ordered chicken, lamb and seafood curry. All delicious! Can't resist eating Indian curry with Nan bread!

The quality of the food at this establishment is truly excellent—a real shame, then, that the front-facing staff seems determined to spoil the entire experience. My recent interaction with an employee concerning a straightforward request was not just disappointing; it was genuinely alarming and insulting.
We were calling ahead simply to inquire about the ingredients in the children's menu items, a critical step because our child suffers from severe food allergies. This wasn't a complex order or a last-minute demand, but a fundamental safety question.
The lady who answered the phone at the front desk had a horrible, dismissive attitude from the very first word. When we specifically asked about the ingredients in the chicken dish to ensure it was safe for our child, her response was shocking. She didn't offer to check with the kitchen, look at a menu, or even suggest a safer alternative. Instead, she offered a cold, callous refusal: "I have no idea. Just eat it or leave it."
This is more than just bad customer service; it's a profound lack of basic human empathy and professionalism. When a customer's inquiry is directly related to a child's health and safety, this kind of nonchalant indifference is intolerable. It sends a clear message that the well-being of their patrons is not a priority.
It is heartbreaking to witness a restaurant pour so much talent into creating genuinely great food only to hire staff who clearly do not give a single thought about service, courtesy, or the serious needs of their guests. What a terrible shame to have a thriving kitchen undermined by such a dismal attitude at the front of house.

So if you want a decent food please go ahead
But customers service, don’t expect a dam

Restaurant: SUNG

FOOD: My friend and I focus on ordering some appetizers, 2 main courses and 1 cocktail (because I don’t drink)

Pork Tacos (Delicious with an excellent and fresh sauce)

Clams: Average.

The fried chicken is the best. The crispy and flavour is spot on. And make our tongue kind of numb.
The noodles are all right, it was good. Nothing fancy. The chicken thigh is very flavourful.

reviews.text: High-quality Taiwanese food with a slightly modern take. The service was super friendly and took their time to explain the menu thoroughly. As a single-diner, it can be difficult to find good Chinese food options because you often need to dine in larger groups. However, here they have a great option to make any Main dish into a set meal (teishoku-style) that comes with seasonal side dishes, soup and a beverage. They also have some smaller dishes that add-on well to the set meal in terms of quantity and price in case you’re hungry or want to try a few more things. For me the real star was the service though, some of the best I’ve received in Taiwan.

A casual lunch short stay in Taichung surprisingly visited this mansion with history since 1929. Building used to belong to a wealth gent with 3 wives all under one roof, but different sections….
Now converted to authentic Tai Wan cuisine, love it!
All dishes in small portion dishes abled us to sample many dishes all new to me except the succulent roast chicken, braised pork knuckles, both delicious, no wonder this place Michelin recommended!
After lunch we stepped to next room the coffee lounge used to be the third wife’s quarter, tranquil & relaxing….
This place really worth visit if you visit Tai chung🥂🥂

Located in Taichung, this restaurant masterfully blends tradition with innovation, offering dishes that highlight the depth and complexity of local flavors while maintaining a sense of elegance.

The menu is a tribute to Taiwan’s culinary heritage, with dishes crafted from high-quality ingredients and executed with precision.

Service is attentive without being intrusive, and the ambiance strikes a balance between modern sophistication and traditional charm. Prices are reasonable for the quality, making it a worthwhile experience for those looking to savor elevated Taiwanese cuisine.

reviews.text: So delicious. Worth the extra trek to get here and so good that after I finished my first one, I got right up and ordered another. Far more tasty than any version you can find in Taipei. I’m definitely a fried bah-wan kind of guy though

Taichung Rou Yuan is a must-visit for anyone looking to experience the rich flavors of traditional Taiwanese street food. This Michelin-recognized stall specializes in Rou Yuan (肉圓, Taiwanese meatball), glass noodle soup, and mochi meatballs, all of which showcase expert craftsmanship and deep-rooted culinary heritage.

The Rou Yuan is the star of the show—its translucent, chewy tapioca skin encases a flavorful pork filling, complemented by a well-balanced sweet-savory sauce. Each bite delivers a contrast of textures, from the tender meat to the slightly elastic wrapper.

The glass noodle soup is a comforting, light broth with silky noodles that pair well with the richness of the other dishes. It’s simple but well-executed, letting the quality of the ingredients shine.

Perhaps the most unique item is the mochi meatballs, which offer a delightful fusion of soft, glutinous texture with a savory umami punch. They’re slightly chewy on the outside but juicy inside, making them an unexpected but welcome twist on a classic meatball.

A [would come again / 還會再來]

· famous traditional taiwanese meatball restaurant thats been around for 80+ years and Michelin-recognized

· just walk in and sit down anywhere with available seat (no service or paper menu here)

· theres air conditioning inside so its summer friendly

· ordered their signature meatball + fishball soup which was around 80 NTD as of June 2025

· meatball had chewy texture while the meat inside tasted delicious + juicy (must add their homemade sauce)

· soup tasted light + topped with their homemade fishballs (honestly it was average)

· food comes within 30 seconds or even faster o.o

tldr: a must come to experience local taiwanese cuisine (with no service)

We went here because this place is in the Michelin list. There are only three items on the menu and we got the fish ball soup and the meatball. The meatball was like nothing I’ve ever had before and I really enjoyed it. The fish ball broth was light and delicious.

Had quite a fair bit of meatballs in Taichung but had to visit this because it is Michelin Bib Gourmand.
Visited the shop at 10am in the morning and they were busy preparing and setting up for business. Their official opening time is 1030am but told me to wait a short while. By 1015am they already asked me to get inside the shop and take a seat and someone came to take my order.
The menu is very simple,  only 3 items for selection. Of course coming here had to eat the meatball and also tried the fishball soup.
Food was served within 2 minutes and first look it was quite pleasing.
First had the meatball. The sauce covered almost the entire meatball you could only see a small bit of it. The sauce tasted very good and smooth and I liked it a lot. What looked strange to me was that the meatball was just filled with the chewy outer layer and there was only meat the size of a ball. It's not really like the typical where the meat filling is consistent across the whole meatball. It quite big, but on the tough side. Not sure if its because it needs to be cooked longer?
Then tasted the fishballs. Wow the fishballs were really good. Can taste the bouncy texture and it feels more closer to a meatball than a fishball. Soup is on the plain side though.
Cheap and rather delicious food. I would say the highlights were the sauce and the fishball. If you like gravy like me, go ask for more. The gravy in the container on the table is the same but it's the spicy version. It might look harmless but it's actually very spicy! It doesn't taste spicy when you put in the mouth but then the fiery kicks in in levels!
Worth a try but maybe go later when the meat are cooked longer.

Fu Kuei Ting is a must-visit for anyone craving expertly roasted goose and silky noodles in Taichung. This Michelin-recognized spot delivers on both quality and flavor, making it well worth the visit.

The roasted goose is the undeniable star—perfectly crisp skin, tender and juicy meat, with just the right amount of smokiness. It’s served with a rich, flavorful dipping sauce that complements the natural taste of the goose without overpowering it. The handmade noodles are equally impressive, with a smooth, bouncy texture that pairs beautifully with the light yet deeply savory broth.

For those who appreciate quality roasted meats, Fu Kuei Ting is a standout. Whether you’re a local or a visitor, this spot deserves a place on your food itinerary in Taichung.

reviews.text:
We had a set, overall is ok.
Love the little cup and at the end I bought a set back home 🥰
Excellent local food reviews.  Good decor. Good value local cuisine and nice service! High lunch traffic and need advanced reservation!
It's a fancy restaurant, you can have some special and different food there, food was okay but I won't go there again, Service wasn’t  great today.

Our initial impression of the restaurant's vibes was okay as we entered, but we were left ignored in the front area for several minutes. At first, we assumed it might be due to a lack of staff. However, a waitress later passed by and treated us as if we were invisible. This gave me a hunch that the service here wouldn't be good. The description of the menu provided by the waitress was quick, impatient, and not easy to comprehend. This might be due to inadequate training or her personal demeanor.

To be honest, some of the dishes here are unique and worth trying. After all, that was the primary reason we came here in the first place (the second reason being its 4.3-star review). The soup was plain and rather ordinary, while the hot pot main course was okay with a tasty broth. The "paper-wrapped rice" main course seemed overcooked but was generously portioned. Surprisingly, both the cold and hot drinks were served before the meals without asking for our preferences, and the hot drink ended up getting cold. As for the cold drink, it had no flavor and tasted like it was made by mixing water and canned jam together. Furthermore, the waiter collected our plates without inquiring if we had finished eating.

Regarding the cleanliness of the dining area, the table was not fully cleaned and felt a bit oily. The total cost for two persons, including a 10% "service fee," was approximately 1,500. Given the quality of service and the overall dining experience, I'd prefer eating elsewhere. If you're considering coming here just to take photos, that might be okay, but for dining, you should think twice before making a reservation.
Pretty consistent quality food

reviews.text: Went on a Monday evening thinking it'll be the least busy and we ended up having to wait for 45mins to be seated. I guess this place is very popular. Dining at a Din Tai Fung in Taiwan was on my to do list and I'm glad I finally had the opportunity to do so. The food was delicious and I can see why. Highly recommend!

Well i got a chance finally to dine at a Din Tai Fung in Taiwan. It was exceptionally good. I had to wait for nearly 60 minutes to be seated. Surprisingly it's the only branch in Kaohsiung and hence it's always packed. The staff were very welcoming and spoke to me in English all throughout. I ordered the prawn cake, pork chop with egg fried rice, spicy cucumber salad and pork and prawn dumpling with in house special sauce. All the food ordered was top quality. Cucumber salad has been a little overhyped by the tiktokers, it's just ok. Also the service was fast. They have mastered the preparation of their fried rice 😍. You need to order it on a app on your phone. I didn't order the Xiaong Long Baos as I have already had it in the past at the DTF branches in Manila, Dubai and Singapore. In Taiwan for some reason they don't give you the spicy chill oil / sauce. But nevertheless a great experience and kudos to DTF for managing the crowd and keeping up the food quality to such high standards in all their branches worldwide.  My bill was around 1025 ntd for all the ordered items.

Never have I ever had such fast and efficient service, food was great to top it off, and no mistakes.

Wish more places take note of how they operate here.

Super clean as well, food is always covered till just before you get it and tables are sanitized after each use.

Plus a cool robot will lead you to your seat.

It was in B1 floor, and super crowded. Even though we were there after lunch time on a weekday, it took us ~100 minutes to wait for our turn. I guess it was because of being the only branch in Kaohsiung. As at the other branches, staff was supet friendly and professional with good English communication. Special thanks to Berry who handled our orders excellently. Beef soup and wonton soup was amazingly tasty. Xiaolongbao was the star!

We were so excited to finally try Din Tai Fung in Taiwan! As regulars at the Seattle location, it felt special to experience it at its home. We ordered two baskets of soup dumplings, the beef noodle soup, and the cucumber salad—some of our go-to favorites.

While we loved the overall atmosphere and were over the moon to be there, we did feel the flavors didn’t quite meet our expectations compared to what we’re used to in Seattle. The beef noodle soup especially tasted a bit bland and lacked the complexity of broth we normally enjoy. The cucumber salad also had less sauce than we’re accustomed to, leaving many cucumbers uncovered, which made it feel less balanced. We also noticed that there weren’t chilies on the table as there are in the U.S. locations—we had to keep asking for them, which took away from the experience a little.

On the positive side, we loved that tea was served consistently and refilled often—it added a nice touch. The service here was excellent, even better than in the U.S. locations. The staff were attentive, warm, and really made our visit enjoyable.

Overall, we’re glad we got to experience Din Tai Fung in Taiwan, even if the flavors didn’t quite match what we’re used to back home. The hospitality made the visit worthwhile, and we’ll always treasure the memory of dining at its original home.

reviews.text:
Perhaps one of the best local Chinese meals I’ve had in a while—simple yet exquisitely prepared with an elegant touch. Good portion too.

The restaurant offers 7–8 course omakase menus at various price points, serving traditional banquet-style dishes with a modern twist.

The ambience evokes the charm of old Chinese/ Western -Japanese colonial times, adding to the overall experience.
Service was excellent although very quick and busy, I’d love to return to explore more of their menu someday.

In 2024, Old New Taiwanese Cuisine was named a Bib Gourmand in the MICHELIN Guide Taiwan.

Highly recommended by locals. Went there on a Saturday and we are lucky to get a table for 3.  Booking ahead is highly recommended.
It is Omakase style and price start from 1K,1.2K and 1.5K. We opted for 1.2K.

Food portion is reasonable and taste not bad. Beef cube is overcooked.

Taiwanese omakase, food overall very good, we had the ¥1500 Menu which had:

1. Sashimi platter - Very fresh and shiok.
2. Prawn w Nian gao - Fresh, niangao soak the flavour of the zhup.
3. Abalone bomb - Tastes like the ocean, can taste the terroir and super delicious.
4. Crab Mee Sua - Wok hey taste very nice, crab also nice.
5. Tiger grouper w lala - Super shiok, I loved it, was steamed in baking paper, cool method I will try next time.
6. Local beef cubes w potato - Nice crispy outer layer, beef itself was so-so.
7. Chicken and fish soup - Good!!!! The fish stomach was very jelly, I like the texture.
8. Smoked bamboo shoot & scallops - Very smoky of course, not overly done and bamboo was still crisp on the outside but soft inside.
9. Taro milk dessert - Damn shiok. Really very good even though I don't like taro.

* We had an incident where the vege was not good and they replaced it with (8). Be sure to voice any dissatisfaction on the spot and the staff will be happy to assist.

Overall can go again if we are in Kaohsiung, not sure if it's a must visit, but it's really good.

Had a wonderful dinner at the Old New Taiwanese Cuisine... We had no reservations but we were given a table...
Food was fresh and tasted exquisite... Would definitely come back when in Kaohsiung

We unintentionally ran into a gem of a restaurant.  When we walked in,they said they were an " omakase " restaurant, so I exclaimed- that sounds japanese than Taiwanese? We were blown away at the quality of service as well as the taste and presentation of each dish! I highly recommend this restaurant. Just be prepared to eat a lot. I wouldn't be surprised if this restaurant gets a visit from Michelin...

reviews.text:
We walked in randomly on a Sunday and they happen to have one table that just became available - I guess that means better to make an reservations on weekends.

Clean, fast, delicious. Price is slightly higher than a daily meal in Kaohsiung, but very reasonable for its setting. Definitely a good choice as a group gathering.

Flavor-wise, it was a little salty and definitely not the most healthy choice. That explains why the food tastes so good 😆

My personal favorite was the eggplant dish - over my expectation and definitely something I would want to order if I’m ever here again.

The staff who seated us I believe was the supervisor, at the table, she inserted her fingers inside the glasses and served it to us, which was extremely unhygienic and not following the food safety rules! Disgusting… not going to drink from the glass!!! Food served was very fast - out in less than 10 mins, delicious, and slightly overpriced but the cocktail took more than 30mins, so don’t bother to order any alcoholic drinks. The limit to dine was 1 hour 20 mins, our table from 7:10pm to 8:30pm, by the time my alcoholic drink arrived, I have finished eating, you judge yourself!

It’s an interesting place. The decoration are cute and authentic, showing Taiwanese culture. The restaurant is very popular, strongly suggest make a reservation before heading.

Their menu has Japanese and English, so probably won’t be a problem for foreigners (if you know those languages).

Their food is authentic and yummy 😋 They have various options. And the portion is not huge. We have a party of three girls, and ordered 5 dishes and 2 rices. I love their eggplants and fried dragon balls! Special and very tasty! A little disappointed for the Lard bibimbap because I feel I didn’t taste and smell the aroma of lard. Water  lotus is also great!

This is a must go place in KS.  Super cool vibe and awesome food and very reasonably priced.   Ingredients were all well picked and could taste its freshness.   It feature Chinese stirred but with a modern twist.   Very professionally made. The eggplant and the sweet and sour pork are must try.  Even the fruit tea was very refreshing.  Servers were helpful and serving was quick.  All youngster and has a great vibe here.   Spacious and even with opened kitchen, it doesn’t smell liked kitchen or those traditional Chinese restaurants. Reservation is needed.

Nice Taiwanese cuisine! We had many dishes, I highly recommend their salted egg with tofu and poached eggs. The service was friendly as well. This restaurant is so good for family and friends gathering！

reviews.text:
This bowl of braised duck rice immediately captivates with its rich aroma. The glossy sauce seeps into the white rice, infusing each bite with layers of duck fat fragrance and savory depth. The duck meat is tender yet pleasantly chewy, retaining its natural flavor, while the bits of braised pork fat add a luscious, salty-sweet richness that’s indulgent but never greasy — truly irresistible from the first bite to the last.

The accompanying offal soup complements it perfectly. The broth is clear yet full-bodied, carrying the essence of duck bones balanced with the gentle spiciness of shredded ginger. Each sip is warm and soothing, with the cleanly prepared duck innards adding both texture and depth.

Overall, this humble duck rice set showcases exquisite craftsmanship — flavorful, comforting, and deeply satisfying. Whether for lunch or a late-night meal, it’s the kind of dish that fills not only the stomach but also the soul.

There was a pretty long line when I went during a weekday lunch hour. I ordered the duck rice with braised pork, and it was good—the duck was tender and juicy, and the pork was nicely seasoned too.

I also tried the dry duck vermicelli, though it wasn’t completely dry—maybe from the sauce or because the vermicelli weren’t fully drained. The flavor was great, but the vermicelli were a bit  mushy for my taste.

The water spinach was just okay, the flavor was pretty average, but still had a nice crunch.

I also had the duck leg, which seemed to be seasoned differently from the duck in the rice. This one tasted a bit bland and under-seasoned.

Even though the restaurant was busy, it wasn’t hard to find a table since people didn’t linger, and the food came out quickly.
Wow, super yum! We ordered braised duck and braised pork on rice, duck glass noodle soup, and braised duck. I highly recommend these three dishes — a must-try! Enjoy, guys!

We had their classic duck meat and pork rice. It was very good, and although not our favorite meal in Taiwan still very worth going out of the way to try. There's always a long line but service is relatively quick and efficient.

Amazing duck rice! it’s sliced duck pieces served on top of braised pork rice. It’s a flavour bomb. Serving is not huge, a large bowl is NT$70, I could probably have 3 bowls to myself. Also tried the duck noodles - it was also good but I prefer it with rice. Environment doesn’t look super clean but it was completely fine. they have toilets available.

reviews.text:
Dumpling Heaven & So Much More! 🤤

Stumbled upon this gem for a late Sunday brunch and wow, what a find! 🤩 We walked in around 11 AM and were seated immediately, which is always a great start to a meal. The vibe is super local and authentic.

Don't worry if your Chinese isn't perfect! The staff are so helpful and will happily mark the order sheet for you. Plus, they have an English menu with pictures so you know exactly what you're getting. 📸 It’s a very chill, self-service setup – you can grab your own little appetizer plates from a cabinet and pour yourself some cold tea or soy milk. So easy! 👍

Now, let's talk about the food. Oh. My. Goodness. The DUMPLINGS! 🥟 They were absolutely divine – juicy, flavorful, and just perfect. Even simple dishes like the fried vegetables with garlic were packed with flavor and incredibly delicious. 🥬🧄

Honestly, everything we ordered was a home run.
This place is a 10/10. It’s a no-frills spot that delivers big on authentic flavor and friendly service. Can't wait to come back for another round of everything! ❤️

A friend’s family took me here.  Without reservation, it will be a super long line to wait.  Must have the sweet pancake, and the free mixed black tea + soy milk.  Totally forgot to take pics.  Very authentic local food.

We walked passed this local restaurant and found a large crowd waiting. We decide to give it a try, for a quick lunch. The waiting was about 15 mins and we shared with another family for a big round table. The foods were yummy. However, two of us got light food poisoning after that.

I visited Hou De Fu Soup Dumplings and Noodles on 28 April 2025 with my boyfriend and had a good dining experience.

The dish we ordered was delicious and freshly cooked, and the portion size was just enough. My favorite is the sweet Pan Cake, Wonton in Spicy Chili Sauce, Hot and Sour Soup, and Fried Pork Ribs – it really stood out.

The service was fast and attentive. The food came out in reasonable time. They offer free drinks in two options: Red Tea and Soy Milk. There's more sauce beside the drink area, too.

The ambiance was lively and everyone is given seats upon entering, with clean tables and comfortable seating.

Prices were fair for the quality of food and experience.

There's a long line during peak hours, so i highly recommend for everyone who wants to try this place to not come hungry. I would definitely recommend this place to others, especially for late lunches and dinners.

For english menu, please look at the photos I provided.

Honestly this is the best restaurant that I went to in Kaohsiung. I stayed in Koahsiung for over a month, tried many places, yet I came back to Hou De Fu around 6 times. Their soup dumplings are a must try, along with their onion scallion pancake and vegetarian green gyozas. The ambience inside is great too, very chaotic in the best way. Service is usually quite good but if you are in a big group or are going there on the weekend make sure you get there early (around 6pm). Thank you so much! I will be dreaming about the food here :). P.s. there is unlimited soya milk, ginger and extremely tasty peanut spice sauce.

reviews.text: Overall this is more of modern style cooking. They may not hit the mark for a 5 but it is a solid 4 and I liked it. Well worth visiting this place.

Personally, I think this restaurant has a great atmosphere with its industrial-style decor. I particularly enjoyed the paintings featuring food and the warm glow of the dim yellow lighting. However, the food tastes average, and I don’t believe it is worth the price.

Tuna with Bread ★★★★★
The bread was perfectly toasted, releasing a delightful aroma that enhanced the eating experience. The tuna sauce, made with both tuna paste and raw tuna, paired wonderfully with the bread.

Grilled Oysters ★★★★★
This was the best appetizer we ordered. Each oyster costs only 65 NT dollars, yet they were fresh and paired perfectly with the cheese.

Seafood Pasta ★
Although it included a variety of fresh seafood like shrimp, clams, and scallops, the linguine was hard, and the flavors didn’t complement the seafood.

Warm Roasted Duck Breast ★
This dish was difficult to chew, because it had many sinews. The waiter explained that they intentionally chose a part with more sinews, but perhaps they should remove them to make the price of this meal more reasonable.

Coconut Milk Latte ★
The flavor of this beverage was a bit off—too bitter and too sweet. The sugar didn’t mask the bitterness of the coffee; instead, it seemed to make it even stronger.

Pineapple Cake ★
This dessert looked delicate, but the best part was the crispy cookie on top. The cake itself tasted average and lacked creativity in its flavor and shape.

The meals are really good and the kitchen is professionnel . However the service is awful: our wine for the appetizers arrived after we finished them and they served the main course with the appetizers. As a result the lamb was cold when we started eating it. The service is not at the level of this good restaurant. Definitely not for picky eaters.

Nice place, good food and a comfortable atmosphere.
The service is friendly and good, however we’ve had to wait for more than an hour to get our food served and after about 45min we’ve been told that some of the ordered dishes were out.
Yes, they did try to compensate us with free desert and in between served salads as apology.

Therefore I had to give 3 stars for the service.
Yes, they’ve handled the situation well, but could manage it better by planning ahead with available portions. As the entire order has to be done online via QR code. So, such things can be planned and no over ordering can occur.

Overall, I wanted to love this place, but there were a few issues that really impacted my experience. Be warned that your favorite dishes might not be available, not even seasonal offerings that could be sold out quickly.

The biggest problem was the incredibly slow service. It took over half an hour just to receive our salads after ordering! We had to repeatedly ask for our drinks.

Wine variety wasn’t much as thought, though by the glass quality wasn’t bad.

The QR code ordering system needs a serious upgrade. Its outdated design and lack of user-friendliness don’t help our already understaffed team. In fact, it adds to their workload.

The overall dining experience was frustrating and fell short of expectations.

Will def be back again soon.

A wonderful dinner. Food and service deserve more than 5 stars.

Highly recommend.

10/10 restaurant!!!!
As good as a Michelin star but half the price! Service is outstanding some of the best I have ever received. Main course wasn’t the best in the world but the other courses, ambiance and service certainly make up for it. Although i’m just a tourist, I would 100% return if i’m ever back in this city. Thanks so much and hope to be back!

The waitress, Carey, had excellent English and went above and beyond with her service. Thanks so much!
l

Service was truly exceptional. Food was delectable. When I expressed that I don't take refined sugar, the staff did their very best to accommodate my dietary requirements and prepared a glass of freshly squeezed juice without any refined sugar for me. They also gifted me a surprise cup of black milk tea with a picture of me and my mom atop since we were there celebrating my qualification as a lawyer in England and Wales. When I said that unfortunately I can't drink black tea due to religious reasons, they asked me if milk might be ok, and when I said yes, they immediately made another one with milk and foam so that I could have it. Overall, it was a truly wonderful dining experience.

We had a great time, the atmosphere is nice with a great decor, the service was excellent: very attentive and friendly event hough it was busy. The food was great, I give it "only" 4/5 because my wife's food wasn't as good as mine. Especially my main course and dessert were just tastier than hers. Other than that, we enjoyed our night out a lot. The staff spoke enough English to have no problems ordering the food as we can't speak Chinese. One tip: a wine cooler would be nice to keep the wine cool during the experience, in Europe that's common practice and I think it would be an easy way to make the experience even better than it already is!

Food quality is so damn good and well-cooked by chef (well done to chef). Sashimi is fresh, drunken shrimp is well-cooked, vinegar pork ribs (陈醋排骨), grilled garlic oyster & Japanese fried shrimp are freaking awesome, roasted duck is nice (too fat & not dare to take more).

Free flow of beers & cocktails are added advantage. Desserts section is really awesome as mentioned from web reviews. Choco lovers' heaven is in the air. A must try dessert Crème Brûlée, smooth & creamy with a perfect burned sugar on top.

Overall, worth to try, price range is fair and affordable.

Came here for afternoon tea buffet.  Even though we had a reservation, we still needed to register at the counter and got a number and waited for our turn to get in.
Food is not bad, like the sashimi that they have salmon and one special fish that were pretty good.  They offered free flow of barley and wheat beer, barley beer was more bubbly and wheat beer was more flavourful.  Tried most of the food, they are above average.

The food here is ok compared to other buffet in Taiwan, they have a large variety of dessert which I really liked. Their drink selection is quite large too. Their service is fast and good.

Ambiance: 4/5
Service: 4/5
Food: 3/5

Definitely a 5 star restaurant...and 5 star price! I'm talking the buffet - not the banquet facilities.
Food: abundant, very good (for the most part) and wide selection - even western dishes. Everything included. They even have a coffee bar that serves some specialty alcohol drinks (I assume are free also). Great dessert selection as well with both Haagen-Dazs as well as gelato.  Wish I had two stomachs!

Service: again, 5. Attendants always around to help clear dishes, help fetch things like a small pitcher of water. Some didn't seem too happy but served well so we thanked them.

Atmosphere: very elegant, comfortable, nice ambiance, not loud at all so we could hear each other talk. Handicapped bathrooms and all areas accessible. They coordinated the flow of people well so no real bottle necks.

The food here is fresh and delicious. I see comments here comparing this buffet to the one in Hanshin Arena but it's no competition. The food here is legit. Pizza is freshly handmade and oven baked on the spot. Sashimi is fresh. There's a gazillion types of little desserts. This place is amazing.

Vegetarian all you can eat buffet located on 2nd floor of Just Sleep hotel.
Variety is less than most of the other buffets that I've had but they do their dishes well. Their dessert section - especially Tiramisu was astandout.

This is by far one of the best vegetarian buffet in Kaohsiung. Very pleasant dining environment, and fast and polite customer service. Foods are always replenish and lots of selection to choose from. Price are fair, they have parking underground, but I suggest to take transit since is located on a busy road. Easy to find. Highly recommend!

The location is on the 2nd floor so you have to go through the tea shop not related ( another company) to the get the lift.
Buffett service. Places are quickly collected from your table when you have finished.
Wide range of Asian ingredients & plates.
Pizza ( freshly cooked) and chips/ fries also offered.
I had bean soup, salad, mixed plate including 3 cups and 100 pages tofu dish and a jelly cube (!?) and tiramisu and a coffee for just under 600.
It was worth it.
You can do DIY Vegetarian Beef Noodles! So delicious!

Wonderful restaurant, loved everything about it. I found it on Happy Cow and I wasn’t disappointed. My 5 and 6 year olds ate for free! The selection is amazing, fresh and well presented dishes with special drinks and desserts that would make any sugar lover crazy. Best meal so far in my visit to Taiwan.

Best restaurant we have tried in Kaohsiung. Overall experience is exceptional and we were really impressed by the lobster!

Was a bit upset at the beginning as we didn’t get seated in time despite the reservation we made while others behind us got seated first.  But the staff was professional in resolving the issue.

Food wise, nothing to complaint and big compliment on the pepper lobster which was perfect. Beef steak was less impressive but decent. Dessert was a nice final touch which served in another area with tea/ coffee and chocolate, pastries offered as well.

Highly recommend to have a try you are already in Kaohsiung!

There was a slight confusion with our reservation but they were able to accommodate us.

The food was amazing! True Michelin star restaurant.

Everything was extremely fresh, creative and delicious. Every dish was amazing. Even the simple garlic rice was out of this world!

Perfect place to celebrate with your loved ones.

Meticulous service- the service is incredible.  From before you enter the Silk hotel, they remind you of the stairs, they push the chairs in for you every time you come back to your seat, the story and introduction to every dish, really makes this place special. The employees are trained to be very ninja like, extremely well mannered, and we don’t even notice when they refill our water, or show up behind us because they’re so quiet.

Amazing quality of food- everything was cooked so perfectly, and well seasoned.  We ordered the wagyu rump and the tenderloin.  Highly recommend to just go for the tenderloin if you’re ordering beef.  It melts in your mouth.  Even when I asked mine to be cooked well done, and it still taste juices, tender, and incredible.  They accommodate all your dietary needs on top of that!

Safe environment - very happy to have gaps between each group even tho we’re seated around the grill, so we’re not too close to other people, and feel safe while dining.

Ukai has a great sense of presenting decent ingredients and dishes. The wagyu is highly praised and live up to the expectation. However, over operated decrease the credit of good meal and teppanyaki. The fried rice is not that traditional and I find it hard to appreciate. Overall a good restaurant, but not for non business situations.
It cost us around usd$270 per person.

We made reservation for weekday dinner to see the skyline of the city around sunset time. Upon arrival we got our table right away, but the overlook view was far more disappointing than expected. They only had few tables by the glass window, couple of them were blocked by the ongoing construction. The overlook view was not great either.

We ordered the preset course for two. The scallop was okay. Seafood risotto was average, the protein was good but risotto was too watery. Same for the ribeye, it wasn’t too flavorful and the bone marrow it came with also had no real taste. The drink, Dr. Kiwi, was good though.

The service was excellent. They had a cube at the table that would notify the servers to order, refill order, clean table and to get check. Very unique way of making the process efficient. I just wish the overlook view and the food was better here.

The restaurant has a wonderful view with high landscapes and provides good service. The waitresses are very friendly and attentive. They offer refills for cake, yogurt, and coffee. However, my experience was impacted negatively when they added pepper to my food despite my request for no pepper, as I am allergic to it. This is a big concern for me. Also, the beef was a bit cold inside, giving me the feeling it was precooked in the fridge and not fresh. Despite these issues, it's still a great restaurant located in the hotel.

Food is beautifully presented and thoughtfully put together. However taste was lacking and not heated enough. Service was friendly and attentive.   Though on the rooftop, not much of a view to see unfortunately. Hotel does not offer parking to diners.

Located at the highest floor of a hotel, this place offer a great view, good good and fun cocktails. Very good dinning experience, like every pasta we tried and love the appetizers. The meat in main dishes are pretty fresh with great sauce. For the cocktails, they offer some interesting special cocktails with different alcohol concentration. Ingredients are clearly recorded on the menu so you can just choose the ones you like. Good dining experience besides that they have clear different menu for dinner time and bar time, so it’s a bit hard for us to find dishes accompanying cocktails after meal. Be sure to book your seats before visit.

Even though the restaurant is pretty small, but I had a great lunch experience here. The lunch set is surprisingly very cheap considering it includes the appetizer, main course, beverage and dessert.
For the main course I definitely recommend pappardelle as it has an amazingly great taste 👌🏻

reviews.text:
Went to Zanlu Chinese Restaurant at InterContinental Kaohsiung to celebrate Father’s Day and ordered their signature roast duck — served in three different ways. Honestly, this is one of the best roast ducks I’ve ever had! The skin was perfectly crispy, bursting with rich aroma and juicy flavor in every bite. The third course, duck congee, was made with so much care — generously packed with tender duck meat and absolutely no bones at all!

We also tried a variety of beautifully crafted dim sum, and every single one was spot on. The braised beef cheek puff was a real standout — flaky, flavorful, and simply unforgettable.

If you’re looking for a special place to celebrate or enjoy a memorable meal in Kaohsiung, Zanlu is 100% worth visiting. Truly an outstanding dining experience from start to finish.

During our recent stay at the InterContinental Kaohsiung, the experience we most looked forward to was dinner at their Cantonese restaurant Zhan Lu – a ritual of ours whenever we check into a five-star hotel.

We had pre-ordered their signature Zhan Lu Roasted Duck, and it exceeded all expectations. When it was brought to our table, the duck trolley was beautifully presented with a wooden box filled with dried flowers – a thoughtful touch that elevated the entire experience and set it apart from other restaurants we’ve visited. It conveyed a real sense of care and sophistication.

The carving was done tableside by the chef, while two attendants assisted seamlessly – one carefully wrapping each pancake, the other serving them to us with grace. The duck skin was beautifully crisp and flavoursome, and the sliced duck wrapped in pancakes was simply divine.

For the second course, we selected the Wok-fried Hand Minced Duck with Espelette Pepper, Pine Nuts, Black Bean Sauce and Lettuce Wrap. It was absolutely delicious – full of depth and texture, especially with the addition of the crispy crackers which added a delightful crunch.

We also thoroughly enjoyed the Wok-fried Rice with Abalone, Seafood, Sakura Shrimps and XO Sauce. It was generously portioned and well-executed, leaving us feeling completely satisfied. Dessert was another highlight – the Taro and Egg Yolk Pastry had a flaky crust with a luscious, lava-like salted egg yolk centre that was simply outstanding.

To top it all off, the restaurant surprised us with a complimentary strawberry matcha cake – a charming and generous gesture. Throughout the meal, the staff were attentive, friendly and highly professional, refilling our tea and anticipating our needs with quiet efficiency.

All in all, this was an exceptional dining experience. From presentation to service and flavours, Zhan Lu truly impressed us. We’ll definitely be returning the next time we’re in Kaohsiung.

Glad we made a point to dine here this evening. The Google reviews were accurate - Andy’s service is exceptional, the ambience is very relaxing, and every dish was delicious while being presented and served with meticulous care.

We ordered the 3-course Peking duck the morning of, but the menu actually advises for 48-hours in advance. I’m not sure if that’s necessary or just recommended.

The duck was juicy and had a very crispy skin. Our second course, the lettuce wrap, was a great choice, and we ended with the congee, which was very smooth and flavourful.

We also enjoyed the giant deep fried egg yolk prawns and water lotus with garlic. Every dish was made to perfection! We thoroughly enjoyed our experience.

Zhan Lu is a perfect spot for a friends and family gathering. Gina and Szu-Chi are super attentive and always ready with great recommendations. Their warm hospitality makes the dining experience even better. Highly recommend!

This is the best Chinese restaurant in Kaohsiung.
It's the most delicious restaurant we've eaten on our family trip.

Special thanks to avery😄

I will definitely visit again!

reviews.text:
Day 1 in Taiwan 🇹🇼
Feeling lucky to start the trip with such an amazing meal — and even better, in a private room! 🍽️ This Michelin-rated restaurant in Kaohsiung serves authentic traditional Taiwanese cuisine, and every dish was outstanding.

✨ The lobster was perfectly cooked and so sweet in flavor.
🍲 The soup, simmered for hours with shark fin, was rich and deeply flavorful.
🍚 The abalone baked rice — absolutely a must-try!
🐟 The locally caught fish was served first as sashimi, incredibly fresh and clean-tasting. The chef then used the remaining meat and bones to fry with salt and pepper — so fragrant and crispy, perfect with a glass of wine or a cold beer. 🍷🍺

Such a memorable dining experience to kick off the trip — a place I’d highly recommend if you’re ever in Kaohsiung for truly authentic Taiwanese flavors! 🇹🇼💫

The restaurant is amazing. Chinese cuisine served here is definitely one of the best I ever had in Kaoshiung. Will recommend for sure if you are ever in the area. Good environment for business meeting and gathering events.

Good meals for my trip!
We wanted to try Taiwan local cuisine and found this restaurant from the Google map. It is definitely fit our tastes with around eight dishes and a dessert which made us spend the wonderful last day of Kaohsiung.
Strongly recommend it!!!

We don’t speak Taiwanese and didn’t have a booking but were given a table by the receptionist who spoke perfect English as did Verin our waitress who explained and served us our meal. We had a set menu of 8 delicious dishes plus a dessert for $1000. It was worth every penny! Both the food and the service in the atmospheric dining room were a treat.

Large space to host many guests. Great interior decor. We got the table on 2nd floor without menu selections. Food quality and taste were great but services need to be improved. We ordered a pot of tea and served without tea cup. Extra order of fried rice and pork rib were served after dessert when we all finished. We came here during long weekend so they are probably short handed. I will come back again on the weekdays not peak season.

reviews.text:
Under the hot weather at 3pm, we ordered the rice and a duck with blue cabbage soup. Bring from SEA, we find Taiwanese food tend to be lighter in flavour and dilution especially in soup. Nevertheless, it was a good experience to have been here .

I limit my opinion only to the orders I made and the others I reserve for another trip in the future.

If you come here, you really only need to order the rice cake and the steamed egg soup. Honestly, the food isn't worth the long queue. While the dishes are good, they aren't spectacular. If you eat in, be careful of the uneven floor outside the main shop area. Overall, it's still worth trying at least once.

This is the street food at its best.  Small menu with 7 items, 5 of them are various style of soups.  The main item - (glutinous) rice steamed in a metal cylindric cup topped with minced pork sauce tastes great that could pair with any one of the 5 soups listed on the menu.  If you would like to take one step further treating your palates, order the black egg.  The egg white part is cooked till it's like, well as it is called in Taiwan, iron egg like.
I don't think the food would be considered a meal like lunch or dinner, but you may enjoy them in any time of the day.  You many either sit inside the restaurant which is not enclosed in walls or outside on the sidewalk.
Since the food place doesn't serve any type of dessert for sweet tooth like me, here is my suggestion:  You can either drive or walk 800 meters to a cool place called "黃家粉圓冰“ nearby on Nenan 2nd Road 河南二路 for some icy & cool goodies.

We ordered the 2 braised eggs, 米糕, bitter gourd pork rib soup and the steam egg soup. All are good!
The meat on 米糕 are very well marinated and makes the 米糕 very tasty.
We particularly like the butterflied pork rib soup - it’s refreshing and helps to clear our taste buds.

Very worth visiting !

It’s an amazing experience eating here—- I think I got climax eating everything tonight… literally everything! My favorite ones were the egg, rice pudding/cake, and steam eggs~ I would recommend people order everything on its menu if you come as like two people! The portion is cutely small. the fish soup and beef soup were alright! Overall, I want to give 5stars to this place! The food is amazingggggg! I love Taiwan!

reviews.text: The food cp value is very high, the food is very cheap but delicious. However, the bags of soup is difficult to unpack and needs to pour into the bowl voluntarily, so I need to get help from the shop owners to pour it. Besides, when I enter the store (seating area), there is a pungent smell as if someone has pooped on the floor. Overall, the store's hygiene is mediocre, the food is bravo, and the shop owners' service is warm.

Yummy Taiwanese favorite staples. Chicken rice (shredded chicken on rice with tasty pork stew sauce), stewed pork belly (with or without rice), raddish, fish balls or meat balls soup.

Can’t go wrong here, usually come here for take out due to difficult parking situation but they also have air conditioned dining area.

No issue with the food all the time I eat here. Lu rou fan, braised bitter melon and bamboo shoot meatball soup today, all very good and cheap! Mid age lady in front taking orders not exactly very friendly as I forgot to write the table number and she refuses to tell me the number after i described to her where I'll be sitting. She made me walk all the way back corridor to see the number. But later the other younger woman who came to collect payment, she was polite and friendly.

Mouthwatering Giant Pork Belly mmmmmhmmmmm. Just thinking about it wants me to go back.

It was so delicious and tender, it just melted in your mouth. Never found another place like this in Kaosiung, so I recommend. There are seats at the back, in case you are worried there is no place to sit.

Also tried the other dishes, and the noodles were surprisingly good. As a foreigner, first time I tried these type of noodles and it’s quite different.

The workers also were kind and had a sense of humour. I will definitely be coming back.

If you’re after braised pork rice, this is it. It’s pretty amazing here. And though the atmosphere isn’t anything amazing, it’s all about the food! The food itself is what shines here, so please keep in mind is is a typical mom and pops style street food. Highly recommended if you’re after with flavor.
Do yourself a favor and have some food from here!!!

A- [it's aight / 還可以]

· famous satay-based hot pot restaurant thats a must go when visiting Kaohsiung for the first time

· its always packed on weekends (avoid peak hours)

· tried their weekday special for 2-person menu which was 980 NTD as of April 2025 (雙人套餐)

· their signature satay sauce tasted strong + fragrant (can choose between spicy/nonspicy)

· hot pot soup was also satay flavored (becomes stronger the longer you cook it)

· seafood here tasted fresh

· my favorite out of all the dishes was their handmade fish + shrimp paste (definitely order)

· the taste became too repetitive after several bites since everything was satay flavored

· theres free herbal tea with good health benefits

tldr: satay lovers will love it here (worth a try but strong flavor)

Our tour guide recommended we try sacha hotpot which is a Taiwanese specialty sauce. He made us reservations which is a good thing because this place was packed and people were waiting outside for a table on a Friday night. There are other locations but this is the main/original one. There are 2 floors and almost every table was full at 6 pm.

We picked the double hotpot broths- Mala spicy and herbal on the other side. The mala broth was pretty spicy. Your mouth gets numb and your nose starts running but it is super tasty. The herbal wine broth was a little odd at first but it grows on you, especially after adding garlic, onions and scallions. There are tons of herbs. Mixing the 2 broths was the best. We got 3 different cuts of meat and my favorite was the ribeye. We also got fried tofu skin, mushrooms, corn, and bok choy and they gave us cabbage and tofu too. The veggies were really good. I didn’t care for the sacha sauce but my friends liked it. We also got some udon.

For 3 people the meal came out to about $23 per person, which is super cheap by American standards, but considered expensive/fancy in Taiwan. Definitely recommend this place for local good hotpot. Bonus- they accept cards which almost none of the restaurants we went to did.

reviews.text: Super good restaurant, with very good vegetarian options if you ask for it: try the scrambled eggs with mushrooms - no idea what mushroom it was, but - fire!
Very nice food and very nice environment. Today also full house, I am lucky as booked table
Good

This restaurant is worth returning to. The private dining experience is truly delicious, each dish perfectly prepared, expertly prepared, and reasonably priced. The braised large intestine goes really well with rice, and the seafood and beef flatbreads are must-try. The pepper shrimp are also incredibly flavorful, and the fried black pig's trotters and German pork knuckle are incredibly crispy—don't miss them. The oysters are large, cooked in a way that removes the fishy smell and preserves the freshness, making them delicious. The Dongpo pork is not greasy, with just the right amount of fat and lean meat. Each dish from the private chef's artisanal kitchen is reasonably priced, and the overall value is excellent. Highly recommended! A must-try for connoisseurs. 👍

I went there a few days ago for a first-time meal, and the dishes I ordered were all quite good. The most memorable ones were the braised chicken feet, the braised pork belly, and the truffle-crusted roast pork. They were flavorful without being too salty, and they went really well with rice. 😊 The bamboo shoots in the scrambled eggs with bamboo shoots were tender and crisp, and the golden sand chicken was perfectly seasoned, with a strong ginger flavor. It wasn't unpleasant, but I wasn't used to it. The restaurant is simple yet atmospheric, but they serve alcohol, so we happened to encounter a table of drunken diners who were talking about obscene things at a loud pace. The restaurant staff seemed to be trying to dissuade them from lowering their volume, which actually dampened our dining experience. If we hadn't been rushing to get away from the unrefined table next to us, we wouldn't have wanted to eat so quickly. 😓
Overall, I liked it and would definitely go back. The customer base and the quality of the food might just depend on luck.

reviews.text: Good vibes 🎅
Nice restaurant

Price: 699 per person, plus service charge.
Meat: Beef, pork, and chicken, all delicious (I usually prefer beef, but the chicken here is so tender and highly recommended).
Dishes: The dishes are clean, but the selection is a bit limited (no pumpkin, taro, mushrooms, etc.).
Main: The Sanuki udon was delicious.
It's rare for sukiyaki to include an appetizer, but it was a great experience.
(The appetizer was scallops on seaweed rice).
The all-you-can-eat restaurant also offers a special: mini burgers. I ate two! (They were delicious, and the burgers were grilled perfectly!)
The dipping sauces are also unique, with four different flavors to choose from, but they're just as delicious without them!
The drink selection is limited... only three... but thankfully there's clam chicken soup.
One downside: The receptionist didn't immediately ask if we had reservations. It took a few seconds for them to speak after we made eye contact, which made me feel a bit cynical...
Overall, it was a very good experience and I'd definitely return.

A Sukiyaki restaurant with its own unique style
(from illustrations to interior design, they are all very cute)
.....
There is only one option for Sukiyaki (soy-grilled)
Each table has a shared pot
....
The meal is a set meal, combined with an all-you-can-eat format
Each person will have an appetizer, dessert, etc.
Meat and vegetable items are ordered through mobile phones
The delivery speed is fast, and there are no missing items
And they don’t worry about you eating too much
The ingredients are really good and full
My friend at the same table said that he would come again because of the peeled shrimp!
.....
In addition to the ingredients that can be cooked, there are also creative dishes from the store. The most distinctive one is the baked barbecue meat plate. Overall, the experience is pretty good

reviews.text:
Felt Truly Welcomed from Start to Finish

I had a wonderful stay at the InterContinental Kaohsiung a few weeks ago. Before my arrival, I had reached out via email, and the team was incredibly thoughtful—they upgraded my room and even arranged a bottle of wine to welcome me. It was such a lovely gesture that truly set the tone for the stay.

The room was clean, comfortable, and cozy, making it easy to relax. The breakfast offered an excellent variety and was absolutely delicious. The restaurant staff were attentive and friendly, and the housekeeping team greeted me with warm, sincere smiles every day.

At check-in, the front desk staff recognized my membership status and welcomed me with genuine kindness and professionalism. Even the fitness center staff were kind and helpful.

Every part of the experience was exceptional, and I’m grateful for the care and attention from the entire team. I’ll definitely be back and highly recommend this hotel to anyone visiting Kaohsiung.

We happened to stay at the InterContinental Kaohsiung. The experience was terrible. We had moved from another hotel, and since Taiwan generally requires an 11:00 check-out, we checked in at 12:00, so we were understandably unavailable for the room。 However, when we returned at 3:00, we saw many guests who had arrived after us already had their rooms assigned, while we were left out and not even offered a welcome drink. Only after repeated requests did we finally get a room.
The room was large, with a nice view and pleasant decor. However, there was dust in many corners, such as the lamp. There were also hair from the previous guest in the drawers. The marble in the bathroom wasn't well-finished, with water stains from construction work in many areas.
The drink coupons were only provided after check-in. Breakfast was also served in the lobby, which was very crowded. The experience was average, and the food was not very tasty. We found a hair in our porridge, but my partner didn't want to bother the busy waiters, so we didn't raise the issue.The way to the pool was like a maze and the AC was on full blast so it was easy to catch a cold.Apart from that, we were very satisfied with the room facilities, especially the smart features. The mattress and pillows were very comfortable.

I stayed with my partner at InterContinental Kaohsiung to celebrate a special day.
As Diamond and Ambassador members, we have experienced InterContinental service in different countries.
At the moment, Taiwan has two InterContinental hotels: in Taichung and Kaohsiung.
We wanted to visit a farther city for this occasion, but after this stay, we felt some regret. Maybe Taichung would have been the better choice.

Good points:
1.	Housekeeping staff cleaned the room very well.
2.	In the Club Lounge, Ms. Lee (short hair) was very kind and thoughtful. Mr. Owen also gave very good service.
3.　The staff at the first-floor bakery were very kind and friendly.

Disappointing points:
1.	The room had a very strong mold smell, probably from the air-conditioning system. Even when the hotel gave us an air purifier, it did not help. The smell made me feel dizzy in the room.
2.	Because it was the weekend, the hotel was very busy. We are Diamond and Ambassador members. At check-in, staff said they could only upgrade us to a high floor. My partner even asked again, “Is this really a high floor room?” The staff confirmed and said, “It’s a Harbour View High Floor Room.” But in this hotel, high floors start from the 11th floor, and our room was on the 10th floor. We can understand the hotel was full, but using this kind of wording to explain made us feel the hotel was not honest.

3.	At check-out, the bill included charges for the minibar. On the first day, we had already asked housekeeping to remove the drinks, because we brought our own wine to celebrate. My partner noticed the wrong charge and asked to correct it, but after the earlier experience, this added more doubt about the honesty of the hotel.
4.	At breakfast, the lady at the reception desk on the first floor was rude. We were surprised that this is the service standard of InterContinental. On the second day, we chose to have breakfast in the Club Lounge instead. At least the lounge was more quiet and comfortable.
5.	The quality of food at both breakfast and the lounge was poor. If a guest had to pay extra for these meals, I would feel sorry for them. The hotel also served some Taiwanese dishes, but if this was my first “Taiwanese flavor” as a foreign visitor, I might not want to try real local food outside later.
Such a great Hotel! It’s on the pricier side but definitely worth it. The rooms are super spacious and luxurious and the staff is friendly and welcoming. Would definitely come again!

I, am Ram Dorji Tamang from the Himalayan kingdom of Bhutan.I had the pleasure of staying at the InterContinental Kaohsiung, Taiwan for five nights, and it was truly an exceptional experience. The services were outstanding, and every member of the staff went above and beyond to make my stay comfortable and memorable. The meals were absolutely delicious, offering a perfect balance of quality and variety. The conference hall was also excellent—spacious, well-equipped, and ideal for professional events.
A heartfelt thank you to the entire team for their warm hospitality and impeccable service. I look forward to returning on my next visit to Kaohsiung!

reviews.text:
Worth going!
Probably the best beef noodle I’ve had so far — high-quality beef, flavorful and tender. The broth is amazing, rich but not greasy. Don’t miss the fresh chili paste — it adds the perfect kick and enhances the beefy aroma even more.
Also, the restaurant is clean and comfortable.

This Beef Noodle is a MUST-TRY! 🔥🍜

If you're in town, you absolutely HAVE to try the beef noodles at 港園牛肉麵! 🤤 This is a legendary local spot for a reason. The broth is incredibly rich and flavorful, and the beef is fall-apart tender. Just pure comfort in a bowl.

Heads up on the process: you order and pay with cash right at the entrance, then snag a table. It's super efficient! We went on a Monday around noon and still had a 15-20 minute queue, so this place is clearly loved by locals. Try to go during off-peak hours if you're in a rush! 🏃‍♂️💨

The portions are perfect for one person, and the price is very reasonable for the quality. 👍 Don't sleep on the side dishes! The cubed tofu and cured cucumber were the perfect companions to the rich noodles. 🥒

Pro-tip: you can grab a drink from the ice tea shop next door to bring in with you!

My only small warning: it can get pretty warm inside! 🥵 On a super hot day, it can be a bit of a sweaty experience. But honestly, for noodles this good? I'd do it all over again. The food is just that worth it. ❤️

This bowl of beef noodle soup is truly impressive. The broth is beautifully clear with a deep amber hue and carries a natural sweetness—likely from slow-simmered vegetables or fruit—that gives it a rich yet refreshing flavor. It’s smooth, well-balanced, and incredibly easy to drink.

The beef is tender and flavorful, cooked to perfection with just the right amount of chew. Each piece soaks up the broth’s essence, making every bite satisfying. The noodles are springy and firm, pairing perfectly with the soup and enhancing the overall experience.

There’s no need for extra seasoning—the original flavor stands strong on its own. What makes this bowl stand out is the distinct sweetness in the broth: gentle, comforting, and absolutely memorable. A dish worth coming back for.

Real enjoyed the beef noodle here. Soup is lighter than other places but packs a flavor punch and is really delicious. Wished they would put in more pieces of beef though but there are lots of side dishes you can get to enjoy while eating the noodles. Would definitely go back again.

This is a popular restaurant so do expect to wait for a table.

I like both their dry tossed pork knuckle noodle and beef broth noodle. Especially the dry noodle, I was impressed by how even aft I left it there like 10 min yet it didn't clump up. The sauce was flavorful yet not oily nor overpowering. The beef broth noodle was equally good though the broth had clean yet flavorful taste. But might be a tad light for some people. Beef tender and a mixture of some tendon and brisket. Noodles springy and beef tendon too had a nice bite, not too tough nor soft, cooked just right. Staff were obviously family like and cordial and polite. Place also decently clean(I sat next to toilet yet no foul smell) But I think a little pricey though. Portion of noodles were generous though.

reviews.text:
We were extremely impressed with this restaurant, so much so that we went there twice just within one weekend.
It’s a lovely Italian restaurant on a regular street; we did not expect the food to be exceptional.
The first time I ordered their lamb shank and it was beyond delicious, meat was tender with great flavors, I ended up putting down the utensils and sucking out the bone marrow because it was that good. My husband got the duck confit risotto, which was full of flavors as well and the rice was cooked al dente!

As for our second visit, we brought a friend with us. I ordered beef cheek and tripe risotto, which was their special of the day and it didn’t let me down one bit, I finished every bit of it on the plate. My husband ordered Matsusaka pork, chicken & sunny egg pasta; the egg was cooked perfectly so when he cut it open, the yolk dripped down into the pasta but he wouldn’t share it with me so I could only imagine how scrumptious it was.
Our friend ordered the spaghetti carbonara, with big pieces of bacon as well as an egg on top, which was outstanding as well and the truffle fries were a good app for sure. Plus, all of the main dishes come with a cup of soup; I’m a soup person so I really loved that.
We will definitely go back when we’re in Kaohsiung again, what a hidden gem and for how good the food was, it was not expensive at all.
We highly recommend this place!

We had a quiet Saturday lunchtime here and enjoyed the delicious food. The preparation was meticulous. The house wine was quite good. The restaurants drinks list includes a selection of four different Belgian premium beers which we might try next time.
Good atmosphere and service. Very mediocre food, risotto was too wet and sea snail tasted bad (stinks). Would not recommend seafood nor risotto at this place.
Presentation, taste, and service are all very good. Nice change of pace if one is looking for something other than the local specialities. Unsurprisingly the seafood is exceedingly fresh.

Authentic food with great flavours! 👍  I like it.

After 1 year:
Tried the same dishes. Chicken is still good, but previously was better. They replaced the sauce with some kind of mustard/horseradish (not a fan).

Whiskey Tiramisu was very watery. Was probably sitting in the freezer for way too long. 😔

Ippon Ramen - Main Store.formatted_address: No. 5號, Yuzhu 2nd St, Sinsing District, Kaohsiung City, Taiwan 800
